# 4. Governance Principles

Classification Governance follows the principles below.

## 4.1 Architectural Authority

Classification shall be governed according to the Documentation Framework architecture.

Governance decisions shall preserve the responsibilities assigned to Classification.

---

## 4.2 Controlled Evolution

Classification shall evolve only through explicit architectural decisions.

Uncontrolled modification of canonical Classification definitions is prohibited.

The corresponding Metadata principle establishes that architectural evolution occurs only through explicit decisions.

---

## 4.3 Traceability

Classification governance decisions shall be documented and traceable.

Every approved, rejected, deferred, deprecated or retired Classification change shall have an identifiable governance decision.

---

## 4.4 Consistency

Governance shall preserve conceptual consistency throughout the Classification architecture.

Family, Type and Class must continue to retain their established responsibilities.

---

## 4.5 Stability

Existing Classification definitions shall remain stable whenever reasonably possible.

Evolution should avoid unnecessary disruption to existing documents and Classification consumers.

---

## 4.6 Transparency

Governance decisions shall be explicit and reproducible.

Implicit governance decisions shall not form part of the canonical Classification architecture.

These principles directly reflect the established Metadata Governance principles of architectural authority, controlled evolution, traceability, consistency, stability and transparency.

---

# 6. Governance Model

The conceptual governance model is:

```text

          Classification Change
                    │
                    ▼

          Governance Evaluation
                    │
                    ▼

          Architectural Decision
                    │
                    ├───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
                    ▼                   ▼                   ▼

                 Approved            Deferred            Rejected
                    │
                    ▼

         Classification Evolution

```

Governance evaluates proposed changes without directly modifying the Classification architecture.

This follows the established governance model in which a proposed Metadata change is evaluated before an architectural decision is made.

---

# 15. Semantic Preservation

Existing Classification semantics shall be preserved whenever possible.

A proposed change that materially changes the meaning of an existing Family, Type or Class shall be treated as a semantic architectural change.

Conceptually:

```text

           Existing Definition
                    │
                    ▼

             Proposed Change
                    │
                    ▼

         Semantic Impact Analysis
         │
         ├── No semantic change
         │
         └── Semantic change

```

Semantic redefinition requires explicit governance.

The Metadata Specification establishes the general requirement that every canonical element have one canonical meaning and that semantic definitions remain stable.

---

# 19. Classification Lifecycle Governance

The Classification Lifecycle defines the conceptual states:

```text

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

Governance authorizes transitions between these states.

Therefore:

```text

            Lifecycle
            │
            └── defines states

            Governance
            │
            └── authorizes transitions

```

This distinction follows the established Metadata architecture: the Lifecycle defines states while Governance authorizes transitions.

---

# 20. Activation Governance

A Classification definition shall not become Active merely because it exists.

Activation requires a governance decision.

Conceptually:

```text

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

          Governance Evaluation
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active

```

The approval criteria depend on the nature and impact of the Classification definition.

---

# 22. Retirement Governance

Retirement represents the end of normal active use.

A Classification shall only be Retired through an explicit governance decision.

Retirement shall not automatically imply deletion of historical references.

Conceptually:

```text

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

---

# 24. Classification Replacement

When a Classification is superseded, Governance may authorize a replacement relationship.

Conceptually:

```text

            Old Classification
                    │
              superseded by
                    │
                    ▼

            New Classification

```

The existence of a replacement does not automatically require historical documents to be reclassified.

Migration decisions must be separately governed.

---

# 25. Classification Migration Governance

Classification migration is a governance concern when it changes the Classification assigned to existing documents.

Governance shall evaluate:

- semantic equivalence;
- historical preservation;
- migration scope;
- impact;
- compatibility;
- validation requirements.

Conceptually:

```text

            Migration Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

             Impact Analysis
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

                Migration

```

---

# 26. Governance and Validation

Classification Validation determines whether Classification conforms to the applicable rules.

Classification Governance determines whether Classification changes should become part of the canonical Classification architecture.

Therefore:

```text

            Validation
            │
            └── "Is the Classification compliant?"

            Governance
            │
            └── "Should the Classification be accepted?"

```

These responsibilities are complementary but independent.

The corresponding distinction is explicitly established by Metadata Governance.

---

# 27. Validation as Governance Evidence

Validation results may be used as evidence in governance decisions.

Conceptually:

```text

            Classification Proposal
            │
            ├───────────────────┐
            ▼                   ▼

        Validation       Impact Analysis
            │                   │
            └─────────┬─────────┘
                      ▼

             Governance Decision

```

Validation does not authorize the change.

---

# 44. Approved

An **Approved** decision authorizes the proposed Classification change.

The change may then proceed through the applicable lifecycle and publication process.

---

# 46. Deferred

A **Deferred** decision means that Governance has not authorized the change at the current time.

The proposal remains unresolved rather than being rejected.

---

# 47. Rejected

A **Rejected** decision means that the proposed Classification change is not authorized.

The rejection shall include a justification.

---

# 48. Deprecated

A **Deprecated** governance decision indicates that an existing Classification definition should no longer be used for new Classification assignments.

The existing definition remains historically meaningful unless a subsequent retirement decision establishes otherwise.

---

# 49. Retirement Decision

Retirement shall be treated as an explicit lifecycle governance decision.

Conceptually:

```text

               Deprecation
                    │
                    ▼

          Retirement Evaluation
                    │
                    ▼

           Retirement Decision
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

The historical definition should remain traceable.

---

# 55. Governance and Publication

Approval and publication are distinct concepts.

Conceptually:

```text

           Governance Approval
                    │
                    ▼

        Publication Authorization
                    │
                    ▼

          Canonical Availability

```

Governance may authorize publication after the necessary conditions have been satisfied.

---

# 56. Governance and Baselines

Classification changes may affect Documentation Framework baselines.

Governance shall therefore identify when a Classification change requires baseline consideration.

Conceptually:

```text

          Classification Change
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

             Baseline Impact

```

The Baseline component remains responsible for baseline management.

Classification Governance does not replace it.

---

# 59. Governance and Automation

Automation may consume or generate Classification information.

Governance shall therefore consider whether a Classification change affects automation.

Automation remains responsible for implementation of automated processes.

---

# 63. Controlled Evolution

Classification evolution follows the principle:

```text

          Existing Architecture
                    │
                    ▼

            Explicit Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

                Evaluation
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

           Controlled Evolution

```

This ensures that the Classification architecture evolves incrementally rather than through uncontrolled changes.

---

# 1. Introduction

Classification is a strategic architectural element of the Documentation Framework.

It provides the semantic organization of documents through:

- Family;
- Type;
- Class.

Because Classification definitions affect the interpretation, organization and discoverability of documents, their evolution must be controlled.

Classification Governance establishes the architectural governance model through which Classification definitions, structures, relationships and lifecycle transitions are introduced, modified, approved, deprecated and retired.

Classification Governance does not define the meaning of Classification itself.

It governs how those definitions evolve.

---

# 10. Introduction of Classification Definitions

A new Classification definition must undergo governance before becoming part of the canonical Classification architecture.

Conceptually:

```text

         Classification Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

         Architectural Evaluation
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

         Canonical Classification

```

The proposal does not become canonical merely because it has been defined.

Governance approval is required.

---

# 17. Classification Relationship Governance

Classification Relationships describe semantic relationships between Classification elements.

Changes to these relationships shall be governed.

Examples include:

```text

            Family
            │
            └── Type

```

or relationships between a deprecated Classification and its replacement.

Governance shall evaluate whether a proposed relationship:

- is semantically valid;
- introduces duplication;
- creates inconsistency;
- affects existing relationships;
- preserves architectural integrity.

---

# 18. Classification Constraint Governance

Classification Constraints establish boundaries on Classification.

Changes to constraints require governance.

The relationship is:

```text

        Classification Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

                Governance
                    │
                    ▼

           Constraint Evolution

```

Validation detects constraint violations.

Governance controls changes to the constraints themselves.

This mirrors the established Metadata model in which Validation identifies violations while Governance controls constraint evolution.

---

# 28. Governance and Classification Dictionary

The Classification Dictionary provides authoritative terminology and definitions.

Governance controls changes to those canonical definitions.

Conceptually:

```text

        Classification Dictionary
                    │
                    ▼

                Governance
                    │
                    ▼

           Canonical Definition

```

A definition becomes canonical only after the applicable governance process has authorized it.

The general Metadata Governance model explicitly identifies approval of Metadata definitions as a governance relationship.

---

# 29. Governance and Classification Schema

Governance controls structural evolution.

Conceptually:

```text

          Schema Change Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

           Architecture Review
                    │
                    ▼

         Compatibility Assessment
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision

```

Only approved structural changes become part of the canonical Classification Schema.

---

# 31. Governance and Constraints

Governance controls the evolution of Classification Constraints.

The relationship is:

```text

                Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

                Validation
                │
                └── detects violations

                Governance
                │
                └── controls constraint evolution

```

This preserves the separation between conformance evaluation and architectural decision-making.

---

# 33. Semantic Consistency

A proposed Classification change must not introduce competing meanings.

For example, governance should reject the introduction of two semantically equivalent Types:

```text

    Type A  =  "Architecture"
    Type B  =  "Architectural Documentation"

```

if both represent the same canonical concept.

The goal is one canonical Classification meaning for each concept.

---

# 34. Duplication Avoidance

Before introducing a new Classification element, Governance shall evaluate whether an existing element already provides the required semantic meaning.

Conceptually:

```text

                 Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

           Existing Vocabulary?
           │
           ├── Yes  ──►  Reuse / Reject Duplication
           │
           └── No  ───►  Continue Evaluation

```

This preserves a coherent canonical Classification vocabulary.

---

# 38. Governance Process

The conceptual process is:

```text

         Classification Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

           Architectural Review
                    │
                    ▼

          Consistency Assessment
                    │
                    ▼

             Impact Analysis
                    │
                    ▼

           Validation Evidence
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

               Publication

```

The established Metadata Governance process follows the same fundamental progression from proposal through architectural review, consistency assessment, impact analysis, decision and publication.

---

# 42. Impact Analysis

The impact of the proposed change is evaluated.

Impact may be:

```text

    Local

```

or:

```text

    Cross-Component

```

depending on its effect on other Documentation Framework components.

---

# 51. Governance Decision Record

A governance decision should contain sufficient information to establish:

```text

            Governance Decision
            ├── Decision Identity
            ├── Proposal
            ├── Scope
            ├── Decision
            ├── Justification
            ├── Impact
            └── Effective State

```

Every governance decision shall be documented.

---

# 52. Traceability

Governance must maintain traceability between:

```text

                 Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

                Evaluation
                    │
                    ▼

                 Decision
                    │
                    ▼

          Classification Change

```

This allows the evolution of Classification to be reconstructed.

---

# 53. Canonical Classification

Only approved Classification definitions become part of the canonical Classification architecture.

Conceptually:

```text

         Classification Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

                Governance
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

         Canonical Classification

```

This mirrors the established Metadata Governance constraint that only approved Metadata becomes part of the canonical architecture.

---

# 57. Governance and Registry

Classification changes may affect Registry entries and discovery.

Governance should identify such impact when evaluating Classification evolution.

Registry updates remain the responsibility of the Registry component.

---

# 58. Governance and Knowledge Graph

Classification definitions may participate in the Knowledge Graph.

Changes to their semantics or relationships may therefore have graph implications.

Governance should identify such impact without taking responsibility for Knowledge Graph implementation.

---

# 61. Governance Constraints

Classification Governance shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 61.1 Explicit Decisions

Implicit governance decisions shall not exist.

## 61.2 Traceable Decisions

Every governance decision shall be documented.

## 61.3 Controlled Authority

Only approved Classification becomes part of the canonical architecture.

## 61.4 Semantic Preservation

Existing Classification meanings shall remain stable whenever possible.

## 61.5 Architectural Consistency

Classification evolution shall preserve the wider Documentation Framework architecture.

## 61.6 Compatibility Preservation

Compatibility shall be preserved whenever reasonably possible.

---

# 64. Architectural Stability

Governance shall protect the long-term stability of Classification.

A short-term improvement should not be accepted when its architectural consequences create disproportionate long-term instability.

---

# 65. Governance Characteristics

Classification Governance possesses the following characteristics.

## 65.1. Authoritative

Governance produces authoritative Classification decisions.

## 65.2. Traceable

Every decision is documented.

## 65.3. Deterministic

Equivalent governance criteria should produce equivalent decisions.

## 65.4. Independent

Governance remains independent of implementation technologies.

## 65.5. Extensible

New governance processes may be introduced without altering the Classification architecture.

## 65.6. Stable

Governance protects the long-term stability of Classification.

These characteristics correspond to those established for Metadata Governance.

---

# 66. Governance Invariants

The following invariants apply:

1. Classification evolution requires controlled governance.
2. Canonical Classification definitions require authorization.
3. Governance decisions must be explicit.
4. Governance decisions must be traceable.
5. Classification semantics must remain stable whenever possible.
6. Governance must preserve architectural consistency.
7. Validation and Governance remain separate responsibilities.
8. Lifecycle states are defined by Classification Lifecycle.
9. Governance authorizes lifecycle transitions.
10. Historical Classification meaning should be preserved.
11. Extensions require governance approval.
12. Governance remains independent of implementation technology.
13. Governance does not define Classification semantics independently.
14. Governance does not modify Classification directly as part of evaluation.

---

# 68. Relationship with Classification Architecture

The relationship between the Classification documents is:

```text

                DF-CLS-001
       Classification Architecture
                    │
                    ▼

                DF-CLS-002
         Classification Concepts
                    │
                    ▼

                DF-CLS-003
           Classification Model
                    │
                    ▼

                DF-CLS-004
         Classification Elements
                    │
                    ▼

                DF-CLS-005
          Classification Schema
                    │
                    ▼

                DF-CLS-006
         Classification Lifecycle
                    │
                    ▼

                DF-CLS-007
        Classification Validation
                    │
                    ▼

                DF-CLS-008
        Classification Governance

```

Governance operates over the definitions established by the preceding documents.

It does not replace them.

---

# 69. Relationship with Subsequent Documents

DF-CLS-008 provides governance foundations for:

- **DF-CLS-009 — Classification Relationships**
- **DF-CLS-010 — Classification Constraints**
- **DF-CLS-011 — Classification Extensibility**
- **DF-CLS-012 — Classification Best Practices**
- **DF-CLS-013 — Classification Dictionary**
- **DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification**
- **DF-CLS-015 — Classification Examples**

In particular:

```text

            Governance
            │
            ├── Relationships
            ├── Constraints
            ├── Extensibility
            ├── Dictionary
            └── Specification

```

---

# 70. Summary

Classification Governance provides the architectural mechanism for controlling the evolution of Classification.

Its fundamental model is:

```text

          Classification Change
                    │
                    ▼

           Architectural Review
                    │
                    ▼

          Consistency Assessment
                    │
                    ▼

             Impact Analysis
                    │
                    ▼

           Validation Evidence
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

               Publication

```

Governance controls:

- Classification definitions;
- Family;
- Type;
- Class;
- Schema;
- Relationships;
- Constraints;
- Lifecycle transitions;
- Extensions;
- Deprecation;
- Retirement.

The fundamental separation is:

```text

            Classification Model
            │
            └── defines what Classification is

            Classification Validation
            │
            └── determines whether Classification conforms

            Classification Governance
            │
            └── determines whether Classification changes
                become canonical

```

Validation answers:

> Is the Classification compliant?

Governance answers:

> Should the Classification be accepted?

This separation ensures that Classification remains a stable architectural component while still being capable of controlled evolution.

# 49. Cross-Component Relationships

Classification Relationships may have implications outside the Classification component.

For example:

```text

            Classification
            │
            ├── Registry
            ├── Discovery
            ├── Knowledge Graph
            ├── Metadata
            └── Automation

```

These components may consume Classification relationships.

However, their internal relationship models remain outside the scope of this document.

---

# 50. Relationship and Metadata

Classification and Metadata are related but distinct concepts.

Classification Relationships describe relationships between Classification Elements.

Metadata relationships describe relationships involving Metadata Elements.

The two models may interact, but one does not replace the other.

---

# 51. Relationship and Document Identity

Classification Relationships do not define Document Identity relationships.

A document may be classified using a Classification Element:

```text

                 Document
                    │
              classified as
                    │
                    ▼

          Classification Element

```

The relationship between a Document and a Classification Element belongs to the document classification mechanism.

The relationships defined in this document primarily concern Classification Elements themselves.

---

# 52. Relationship and Registry

The Registry may expose Classification Relationships for discovery.

However:

```text

            Classification Relationships
            │
            └── defines semantic relationship

            Registry
            │
            └── exposes registered relationship information

```

The Registry does not redefine Classification semantics.

---

# 53. Relationship and Knowledge Graph

Classification Relationships may become edges in a Knowledge Graph.

Conceptually:

```text

          Classification Element
                    │
               relationship
                    │
                    ▼

          Classification Element

```

may be represented as:

```text

            Node  ─────  Edge  ─────►  Node

```

The Knowledge Graph is an external representation and discovery mechanism.

The Classification Relationship remains the authoritative semantic definition.

---

# 61. Relationship Historical Preservation

Historical relationships should remain interpretable.

When a relationship is deprecated or retired, its historical meaning should remain available where necessary.

For example:

```text

                Old Class
                    │
               replaced by
                    │
                    ▼

                New Class

```

preserves the evolution of the Classification model.

---

# 63. Relationship Impact

Relationship changes may have local or cross-component impact.

Examples:

| Change | Potential Impact |
|--------|------------------|
| New relationship | Local / Dictionary / Validation |
| Changed cardinality | Schema / Validation |
| Changed relationship semantics | Entire Classification architecture |
| Deprecated relationship | Existing Classification |
| Retired relationship | Historical data |
| New inverse | Navigation / Discovery |
| New cross-component relationship | Registry / Knowledge Graph |

Impact shall be evaluated before approval.

---

# 13. Classification Hierarchy

The primary hierarchy can therefore be represented as:

```text

            Family
            │
            ├── Type
            │   ├── Class
            │   ├── Class
            │   └── Class
            │
            ├── Type
            │   ├── Class
            │   └── Class
            │
            └── Type

```

This hierarchy provides the structural organization of Classification.

---

# 20. Relationship Cardinality

A Classification Relationship may impose cardinality constraints.

For example:

```text

            Family 1  ─────  * Type
            Type   1  ─────  * Class

```

This represents the conceptual model in which:

- a Family may contain multiple Types;
- a Type belongs to a Family;
- a Type may contain multiple Classes;
- a Class belongs to a Type.

The exact cardinality constraints are subject to the Classification Schema and Classification Specification.

---

# 43. Acyclicity

Hierarchical Classification relationships should preserve an acyclic structure.

For example:

```text

                  Family
                    │
                    ▼

                   Type
                    │
                    ▼

                  Class

```

must not result in:

```text

                  Family
                    │
                    ▼

                   Type
                    │
                    ▼

                  Class
                  │
                  └────────► Family

```

when the relationship type is hierarchical and acyclic.

Cycles shall be treated as invalid where prohibited by the Classification Schema.

---

# 17. Hierarchy Acyclicity

The Classification hierarchy shall not contain prohibited cycles.

For example, the following is invalid:

```text

                  Family
                    │
                    ▼

                   Type
                    │
                    ▼

                  Class
                  │
                  └────────► Family

```

when the relationships are hierarchical.

A hierarchical Classification structure must remain acyclic.

---

# 31. Lifecycle Constraints

Classification Lifecycle defines the states through which Classification Elements may evolve.

The conceptual lifecycle is:

```text

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

Classification Elements shall respect the rules applicable to their current lifecycle state.

---

# 32. Defined State

A Classification Element in the `Defined` state has been formally defined but is not necessarily available for normal active use.

It shall not be treated as Active unless the applicable lifecycle transition has occurred.

---

# 33. Active State

An Active Classification Element may be used according to its definition and applicable Classification rules.

Only valid and authorized Classification Elements may be Active.

---

# 34. Deprecated State

A Deprecated Classification Element shall not normally be used for new Classification assignments.

Existing historical uses may remain valid.

Deprecation shall preserve historical interpretation.

---

# 35. Retired State

A Retired Classification Element shall no longer be used as an active Classification Element.

Historical references may remain necessary for traceability.

Retirement shall not automatically imply deletion.

---

# 36. Lifecycle Transition Constraints

Classification Elements shall only undergo permitted lifecycle transitions.

For example:

```text

            Defined     ─────►  Active
            Active      ─────►  Deprecated
            Deprecated  ─────►  Retired

```

An invalid transition shall be rejected.

Governance authorizes lifecycle transitions.

Validation verifies that an observed lifecycle state conforms to the permitted lifecycle.

---

# 42. Non-Destructive Evolution

Classification evolution should prefer changes that preserve existing information.

For example:

```text

            Old Classification
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

               Replacement

```

is preferable to silently deleting the old Classification when historical traceability is required.

---

# 43. Migration Constraints

When Classification changes require migration, the migration shall preserve historical meaning.

A migration shall not silently convert historical Classification into a new semantic interpretation.

Where necessary, the original Classification shall remain traceable.

---

# 78. Relationship with Classification Lifecycle

Classification Lifecycle defines lifecycle states and transitions.

Classification Constraints defines restrictions applicable to those states and transitions.

Therefore:

```text

            Classification Lifecycle
            │
            └── defines lifecycle behavior

            Classification Constraints
            │
            └── constrains lifecycle behavior

```

---

# 46. Validation Responsibility

Classification Validation is responsible for identifying constraint violations.

It may determine that:

```text

                Constraint
                    │
                    ▼

          Satisfied / Violated

```

Validation does not modify the constraint.

---

# 53. Constraint Conflicts

Two constraints shall not establish contradictory requirements.

For example:

```text

    Constraint A:
    Type must belong to exactly one Family.

    Constraint B:
    Type may belong to multiple Families.

```

cannot both be canonical without an explicit contextual distinction.

Constraint conflicts must be resolved through Governance.

---

# 54. Constraint Precedence

Where multiple constraints apply, their relationship and precedence shall be explicitly defined by the Classification Specification.

An implementation shall not invent precedence rules when the canonical architecture does not define them.

---

# 56. Constraint Applicability

A constraint applies only when its applicability conditions are satisfied.

Conceptually:

```text

          Classification Element
                    │
                    ▼

              Applicability
              │
              ├── Not Applicable
              │
              └── Applicable
                      │
                      ▼

                  Evaluation

```

This prevents unrelated constraints from being applied universally.

---

# 58. Violation Identification

Constraint violation identification belongs to Classification Validation.

Conceptually:

```text

              Classification
                    │
                    ▼

          Constraint Evaluation
          │
          ├── Compliant
          │
          └── Violation
```

---

# 59. Violation Resolution

The resolution of architectural constraint violations belongs to Classification Governance where a governance decision is required.

For example:

```text

                Violation
                    │
                    ▼

          Governance Evaluation
          │
          ├── Correct
          ├── Accept temporarily
          ├── Deprecate
          └── Reject

```

Validation identifies.

Governance decides.

---

# 79. Relationship with Classification Validation

Classification Validation evaluates whether Classification satisfies the constraints.

Therefore:

```text

        Classification Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

        Classification Validation
                    │
                    ▼

            Conformance Result

```

Validation does not redefine the constraints.

---

# 45. Governance Constraint

Classification Constraints themselves shall evolve only through Classification Governance.

The relationship is:

```text

        Classification Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

        Classification Validation
        │
        └── detects violations

        Classification Governance
        │
        └── controls constraint evolution

```

This preserves the established separation between validation and governance. The analogous Metadata architecture explicitly states that Validation identifies violations while Governance resolves them and controls constraint evolution.

---

# 4. Extensibility Principles

Classification Extensibility follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Stability

Extensions shall preserve the stability of the Classification architecture.

An extension shall expand the architecture rather than undermine its foundations.

---

## 4.2. Semantic Preservation

Extensions shall preserve the established meaning of existing Classification Elements.

An extension shall not silently redefine an existing Family, Type or Class.

---

## 4.3. Structural Preservation

Extensions shall remain compatible with the canonical Classification structure.

New elements shall occupy positions permitted by the Classification Schema.

---

## 4.4. Backward Compatibility

Extensions should preserve the validity and interpretation of existing Classification whenever reasonably possible.

Existing documents should not become semantically ambiguous merely because Classification evolves.

---

## 4.5. Canonical Preservation

Extensions shall remain part of one canonical Classification architecture.

Independent competing Classification models shall not be introduced as extensions.

---

## 4.6. Technology Independence

Extension mechanisms shall remain independent of:

- programming languages;
- databases;
- repositories;
- serialization formats;
- implementation frameworks.

---

## 4.7. Controlled Evolution

Classification extensions shall be introduced through the applicable governance process.

An extension becomes canonical only after approval.

---

# 7. Extensible Classification Elements

The following Classification artifacts may be extended.

## 7.1. Classification Families

New Families may be introduced when a new high-level Classification domain is required.

An existing Family shall not be redefined to represent an unrelated domain.

---

## 7.2. Classification Types

New Types may be introduced within existing Families.

A new Type shall have a defined semantic relationship with its containing Family.

---

## 7.3. Classification Classes

New Classes may be introduced within existing Types.

A new Class shall comply with the semantic and structural constraints of its Type.

---

## 7.4. Classification Relationships

New relationship types may be introduced when an architectural requirement cannot be adequately represented by the existing relationship vocabulary.

Relationship extensions shall define:

- semantics;
- direction;
- source;
- target;
- cardinality;
- constraints;
- lifecycle implications.

---

## 7.5. Classification Schema

The Classification Schema may evolve through the controlled introduction of new structural capabilities.

Existing structural definitions shall remain valid whenever reasonably possible.

---

## 7.6. Classification Dictionary

The Classification Dictionary may be extended through the addition of newly approved Classification definitions.

Existing canonical definitions remain authoritative unless explicitly changed through governance.

---

## 7.7. Classification Specification

The Classification Specification may evolve to incorporate approved Classification extensions.

The Specification remains the normative integration point for the resulting Classification architecture.

---

# 8. Extension Categories

Classification extensions may belong to one of the following categories.

## 8.1. Additive Extension

Introduces new Classification Elements without changing the meaning of existing elements.

Example:

```text

            Existing Classification
            │
            ├── Family A
            │
            └── Family B

```

becomes:

```text

            Existing Classification
            │
            ├── Family A
            ├── Family B
            └── Family C   ←  Added

```

Additive extension is the preferred extension mechanism.

---

## 8.2. Specialization Extension

Introduces a more specific Classification Element within an existing semantic context.

For example:

```text

            Family
            │
            └── Type
                │
                └── New Class

```

The specialization must preserve the semantics of the parent context.

---

## 8.3. Structural Extension

Introduces an approved structural capability into the Classification Schema.

Structural extensions shall not invalidate existing Classification without explicit governance.

---

## 8.4. Relationship Extension

Introduces a new canonical relationship type.

For example:

```text

            Element A  ─────  newRelationship  ─────►  Element B

```

The new relationship shall have explicit semantics and constraints.

---

## 8.5. Dictionary Extension

Introduces new entries into the Classification Dictionary.

Dictionary extensions shall correspond to approved Classification concepts.

---

## 8.6. Specification Extension

Introduces normative requirements associated with an approved Classification capability.

---

## 8.7. Evolutionary Extension

Introduces a controlled refinement of the Classification architecture.

Evolutionary extensions may affect existing definitions and therefore require explicit impact analysis and governance.

---

## 4.2. Semantic Preservation

Extensions shall preserve the established meaning of existing Classification Elements.

An extension shall not silently redefine an existing Family, Type or Class.

---

## 4.4. Backward Compatibility

Extensions should preserve the validity and interpretation of existing Classification whenever reasonably possible.

Existing documents should not become semantically ambiguous merely because Classification evolves.

---

## 7.2. Classification Types

New Types may be introduced within existing Families.

A new Type shall have a defined semantic relationship with its containing Family.

---

## 7.3. Classification Classes

New Classes may be introduced within existing Types.

A new Class shall comply with the semantic and structural constraints of its Type.

---

## 8.7. Evolutionary Extension

Introduces a controlled refinement of the Classification architecture.

Evolutionary extensions may affect existing definitions and therefore require explicit impact analysis and governance.

---

# 23. Lifecycle Compatibility

Extensions shall integrate with the Classification Lifecycle.

A new Classification Element shall have an applicable lifecycle state.

Its lifecycle shall be governed in the same manner as existing Classification Elements.

Extensibility and lifecycle are complementary but independent concerns.

---

# 38. Extension Lifecycle

Extensions may themselves have a lifecycle:

```text

                 Proposed
                    │
                    ▼

               Under Review
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

The lifecycle state of an extension does not replace the lifecycle state of the Classification Elements introduced by it.

---

# 41. Extension Retirement

A retired extension is no longer part of the active Classification architecture.

Historical information associated with the extension should remain interpretable when necessary.

---

# 42. Non-Destructive Evolution

Classification evolution should prefer non-destructive mechanisms.

For example:

```text

         Existing Classification
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

               Replacement

```

is preferable to silently deleting an existing Classification Element when historical traceability is required.

---

# 43. Extension Compatibility with Historical Classification

An extension shall not make historical Classification unintelligible.

For example:

```text

           Historical Document
                    │
                    ▼

        Historical Classification
                    │
                    ▼

            New Classification

```

The new Classification may provide a replacement or supersession path without erasing the historical meaning.

---

# 35. Approved Extension

An approved extension becomes part of the canonical Classification architecture.

Conceptually:

```text

            Extension Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Approval
                    │
                    ▼

Canonical Classification

```

Before approval, the extension remains a proposal.

---

# 36. Rejected Extension

A rejected extension shall not become part of the canonical Classification architecture.

The rejection should preserve its rationale where governance traceability requires it.

---

Classification provides the semantic organization through which documents are grouped into meaningful categories.

Within the Documentation Framework, Classification supports:

- organization;
- navigation;
- governance;
- discovery.

Classification is independent of the physical location of documents.

The Classification architecture therefore requires more than a formal model.

It also requires practices that preserve semantic clarity, structural consistency, maintainability and long-term architectural integrity.

Classification Best Practices defines recommended practices for designing, using, maintaining and evolving the Classification component.

This document is **informative**.

It provides guidance rather than introducing additional normative requirements beyond those established by the Classification architecture, constraints and specification.

# 1. Introduction

This document constitutes the normative specification of the Classification component within the Documentation Framework.

It consolidates the architectural principles, concepts, model, elements, schema, lifecycle, validation, governance, relationships, constraints, extensibility and terminology defined throughout the Classification documentation family into a single authoritative specification.

This document defines the contractual requirements that every Classification implementation shall satisfy in order to conform to the Documentation Framework.

Classification is an architectural mechanism for organizing documents according to meaningful semantic categories.

It is independent of physical document storage, implementation technology and repository structure.

---

## 6.1. R-001 — Architecture Compliance

Classification shall conform to the Classification Architecture defined by DF-CLS-001.

Classification implementations shall not introduce architectural responsibilities that contradict the Classification Architecture.

---

## 6.4. R-004 — Classification Model Compliance

Classification structures shall conform to the Classification Model defined by DF-CLS-003.

The model shall remain consistent with the conceptual foundation established by the Documentation Framework.

---

## 6.6. R-006 — Schema Compliance

Classification structures shall conform to the applicable Classification Schema defined by DF-CLS-005.

Schema requirements shall not be bypassed by implementation-specific behavior.

---

## 6.7. R-007 — Hierarchical Consistency

Where Classification uses hierarchical relationships, parent-child relationships shall represent meaningful semantic specialization.

An implementation shall not create artificial hierarchy solely for physical or technical convenience.

---

## 6.10. R-010 — Classification Assignment

A Classification assignment shall reference only valid Classification Elements defined by the applicable Classification Schema.

An assignment shall not introduce an undefined Classification concept.

---

## 6.13. R-013 — Cardinality Compliance

Classification assignments and relationships shall respect the cardinalities defined by the Classification Schema and Classification Constraints.

---

# 7. Semantic Requirements

Classification shall satisfy the following semantic requirements.

- Every canonical Classification Element shall possess one canonical meaning.
- Classification definitions shall remain stable.
- Equivalent Classification concepts shall not coexist without explicit semantic justification.
- Classification terminology shall remain consistent.
- Classification interpretation shall be deterministic.
- Classification relationships shall have explicit meanings.
- Hierarchical relationships shall represent meaningful semantic specialization.
- Classification shall remain independent of physical document organization.
- Classification shall remain independent of implementation technology.

These requirements derive from the Framework's requirement that architectural concepts be clearly defined, independent, stable, reusable and explicit.

---

# 8. Structural Requirements

Classification structures shall satisfy the following requirements.

## 8.1. Valid Elements

Every element shall be defined by the Classification model.

## 8.2. Valid Hierarchy

Every hierarchical relationship shall be structurally valid.

## 8.3. Valid Relationships

Every relationship shall conform to its defined relationship type.

## 8.4. Valid Cardinality

All applicable cardinality constraints shall be satisfied.

## 8.5. No Orphaned Canonical Elements

Every canonical Classification Element shall have a valid structural context unless the Classification Model explicitly defines it as an independent root element.

## 8.6. No Undefined References

Classification assignments and relationships shall not reference undefined elements.

---

## 6.5. R-005 — Element Compliance

Every Classification Element shall satisfy the characteristics defined by DF-CLS-004.

A Classification Element shall possess an identifiable semantic meaning.

---

## 6.20. R-020 — Semantic Stability

The semantic meaning of an active Classification Element shall remain stable.

A change that materially alters the meaning of an existing Classification Element shall be treated as an architectural change.

---

## 6.21. R-021 — Deprecation

A Classification Element that is no longer recommended for new use shall be capable of being placed into a deprecated lifecycle state.

Deprecation shall not silently erase historical Classification assignments.

---

## 6.22. R-022 — Historical Preservation

Historical Classification information shall be preserved where necessary to maintain the interpretation of previously established documentation.

Retirement shall not automatically imply deletion of historical meaning.

---

## 6.25. R-025 — Non-Destructive Validation

Validation shall not modify the Classification structure being evaluated.

Validation determines compliance; it does not silently correct the Classification model.

---

## 6.26. R-026 — Governance

Classification evolution shall occur only through the governance mechanisms defined by DF-CLS-008.

Significant architectural Classification changes shall be explicitly reviewed and approved.

---

## 6.27. R-027 — Governance Traceability

Governance decisions affecting Classification shall be documented and traceable.

The historical record shall identify the relevant change and decision.

---

## 6.29. R-029 — No Silent Redefinition

A Classification extension shall not silently redefine the meaning of an existing canonical Classification Element.

Semantic redefinition shall constitute an explicit architectural change.

---

## 6.30. R-030 — Backward Compatibility

Classification evolution shall preserve backward compatibility whenever reasonably possible.

Where compatibility cannot be preserved, the impact shall be explicitly identified and governed.

---

# 9. Lifecycle Requirements

Classification shall evolve according to DF-CLS-006.

Lifecycle transitions shall:

- be explicit;
- conform to the defined lifecycle;
- be traceable;
- respect governance;
- preserve historical meaning.

A typical lifecycle may be represented conceptually as:

```text

                 Proposed
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

The exact lifecycle states and transitions are defined by the Classification Lifecycle document.

---

## 6.24. R-024 — Deterministic Validation

Classification validation shall be:

- deterministic;
- repeatable;
- non-destructive.

The same Classification structure evaluated against the same rules shall produce an equivalent validation result.

---

# 33. Requirement Identification

Normative requirements are identified using the following format:

```text

    R-001
    R-002
    R-003
    ...

```

Requirement identifiers shall remain stable within a specification version.

When a requirement is removed or substantially redefined, its historical status shall remain traceable.

---

# 34. Requirement Interpretation

The following terms indicate normative strength:

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **shall** | Mandatory requirement |
| **shall not** | Mandatory prohibition |
| **should** | Recommendation unless a justified exception exists |
| **may** | Permitted behavior |
| **informative** | Non-normative guidance |

The terms **shall** and **shall not** identify mandatory requirements.

---

| Component | Relationship |
|-----------|--------------|
| Document Identity | Consumes Metadata to describe document identity. |
| Classification | Consumes Metadata to organize documents. |
| Templates | Define how Metadata is represented in documents. |
| Workflow | Consumes Metadata during lifecycle management. |
| Policies | Uses Metadata for governance decisions. |
| Baselines | Preserve Metadata across framework evolution. |
| Registry | Indexes Metadata for document discovery. |
| Relationships | Connect Metadata across architectural entities. |
| Knowledge Graph | Uses Metadata as semantic nodes and properties. |
| Validation | Verifies Metadata compliance. |
| Automation | Produces and consumes Metadata during automated processes. |

---

# 13. Architectural Evolution

The Metadata component evolves incrementally according to the Metadata Roadmap.

Its evolution follows the progression:

1. Core Metadata
2. Structural Metadata
3. Lifecycle Metadata
4. Governance Metadata
5. Traceability Metadata
6. Discovery Metadata
7. Automation Metadata

Each stage extends the Metadata architecture without redefining previously established concepts.

# 4. Scope

The component's scope includes identity concepts, models, elements/schema, constraints, identity lifecycle, validation, governance, typed relationships, assessed extensibility, specifications and examples. Detailed sources retain their responsibilities; this architecture does not invent a canonical merged field catalog or certify all peer requirements.

For applicable normalized documents, logical identity remains associated with the same document across ordinary content/descriptor, classification, representation, repository and document-edition changes. Exact edition coordinates, document Status, identity-record assignment/preservation/retirement evidence, maturity and Baseline membership are separate facts. A mutable state record is not a replacement for the stable identity key.

Unassigned concerns a pre-allocation subject, not an already assigned Domain+Identifier key. Retirement preserves allocated-number reservation, document association/history and reference interpretation; it does not guarantee a running resolver or retrievable content. Document lifecycle and identity-record lifecycle can have distinct subjects/contracts. The source does not prescribe a universal transition or permission graph.

DID-003/004/005/006/010/014 currently disagree on reference cardinality, mandatory State/Canonical Reference fields and identity state terminology. Those actual claims are preserved in §12.3 for full owner cycles. The architectural distinctions here neither merge incompatible schemas nor silently remove/add their mandatory fields. No Metadata Dictionary Element, Profile or canonical state record is fabricated.

---

# 5. Out of Scope

The following roles are separate from document identity semantic ownership. Area labels, registered capability contracts and operational executors are identified separately; naming an owner proves no implemented service.

| Received responsibility | Responsible contract/role | Operational or semantic boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Document metadata | Metadata plus applicable semantic domain owners | Dictionary defines, Schema organizes, Profile constrains and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile; descriptive representation does not replace identity |
| Document classification | Classification | Family/Type and other category meanings remain mutable and separately owned |
| Registry management | Registry | Catalog/lookup contracts and provenance; actual registration/lookup executed by an applicable system/process |
| Discovery services | Discovery area: Registry, Relationships, Knowledge Graph, Navigation, Search | Area groups capabilities; it is not another component or mandatory routing intermediary |
| Workflow management | Workflow and applicable Policies | Subject-specific transitions/rules; DMS/tool/manual operation, not an implemented DF workflow engine |
| Version control | Documentary edition contracts versus source-control systems/adapters | Version/Revision/Status semantics follow applicable governance/edition contracts; repository commits and Source Control Integration adapters do not define them |
| Repository management | DMS or other applicable external system | Organization, storage, permissions and physical-location execution |
| Storage technologies | Applicable implementations/external systems | Persistence mechanisms preserve applicable representation/provenance requirements |
| Identifier generation algorithms | Applicable allocation executor | Generate/allocate under identity-domain rules and collision/reservation evidence; no algorithm supplied here |
| Persistence mechanisms | Applicable implementation/external system | Store identity/edition/context records without acquiring identity semantics |

Governance is an area grouping Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines; it is not a single invented component owning all operational management. Reviews records examined scope/results; Baselines defines immutable selected exact approved editions and context. CMS change evidence does not substitute for documentary approval or snapshot inclusion.

---

# 7. Core Architectural Characteristics

Within its declared allocation/preservation contract, an assigned logical identity shall be unique for the document in its domain, stable through normal evolution, and never reassigned to a different document. Domain qualification is required to interpret uniqueness; an identifier string alone is not universally unique across unregistered domains.

Immutability concerns the assigned Domain+Identifier key under its applicable contract, not every mutable record about that identity. Identity-state evidence, references, location, descriptors and exact-edition coordinates can evolve under their own owner rules without automatically replacing the key. References and aliases interpret an existing logical document; they do not license another document to reuse its identity. Allocated and retired identities remain reserved.

Preserve valid assigned identity during ordinary classification, repository, format, lifecycle and edition changes. If a necessary authorized schema/ID migration would change an otherwise immutable representation/allocation contract, first assess and explicitly reconcile the governing previous/new rules with responsible identity/domain sources. Record old→new mappings, same-document continuity, aliases/reservations, collisions, historical/reference/context effects, exact source editions, affected consumers and transition verification before coordinated application. Preserve original representations and historical immutable snapshot selections; never retarget old members or reassign retired allocations to another document. No blanket permission for arbitrary identity changes or two contradictory governing rules for one operation is introduced. This localized UPDATE performs no migration.

Long-term understandable/referenceable identity is a requirement and design objective supported by qualified domain/canonicalization and actual preservation/resolution evidence. It guarantees neither universally understood bare strings nor future content availability. Exact-edition references additionally identify the intended Version/Revision and relevant bytes/context; logical identity alone selects neither an exact edition nor Baseline membership.

---

# 9. Component Relationships

The following are scoped architectural contract declarations for documentary uses. They do not establish an operational service call, every-component routing requirement or complete dependency graph.

| Consumer | Provider | Required contract/use | Source/scope boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metadata | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document described | DID-009 §5.1 declaration; descriptive values retain their own semantic owners |
| Classification | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document being classified | DID-009 §5.2; category/definition entity identity is a separate qualified contract |
| Templates | Document Identity | Identity of normalized Template documentation/document instances | DID-009 §5.3; Template definition/instance keys are not automatically DF document IDs |
| Registry | Document Identity | Logical document identity for a document catalog entry | DID-001 §9.4; source-edition provenance and exact lookup context required |
| Relationships | Document Identity | Identity of document endpoints | DID-001 §9.5; other endpoint kinds use their own domain contracts |
| Knowledge Graph | Document Identity | Logical document node identity | ARC-005 §12; typed edges remain Relationships records, not document identities |
| Baselines | Document Identity | Logical member identity | ARC-005 §12; exact edition/descriptive/context evidence additionally required |
| Workflow | Document Identity | Identified normalized document subject | DID-009 §6.1; applicable transition execution remains with the actual process |

## 9.1. Metadata

Identity identifies the logical document; Metadata defines/represents descriptors and owner meanings. Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles remain separate under one effective Profile. Identity data can be represented descriptively without transferring identity semantics or creating missing Metadata Element/catalog records.

**Unresolved reciprocal declarations:** supplied README states Document Identity→Metadata for descriptive concepts, while DID-009 §§5/10 states Metadata→Document Identity and no dependency on consuming components. Both source claims remain visible as required-dependency evidence pending owner/context/interface reconciliation. Distinguish core identity meaning from identity-record descriptor use, but do not silently downgrade a genuinely required contract into navigation or declare the apparent cycle resolved. Different stated uses alone do not prove operational independence or global acyclicity. Full Metadata/DID source cycles must establish the actual required scopes and cycle treatment under ARC-004.

## 9.2. Classification

Classification owns category meanings and uses identity when categorizing a normalized document. Current Family/Type/Component labels are independent from stable allocation series and do not automatically reconstruct an assigned valid ID. Classification definitions and their own lifecycle/keys are different subjects from document editions; their actual identity contracts need qualification. Nominal CLS-003/CLS-001 collision reconciliation remains scheduled, not corrected by this source.

## 9.3. Templates

Templates owns reusable documentary structures and definition/instance contracts. A normalized document describing or applying a Template can require document identity; Template entities and graph/relationship identifiers are not thereby allocated normalized document IDs. Templates consumes appropriate owner meanings without redefining document identity, Metadata or Classification. Source presence and using a Template prove neither consistency nor approved publication.

## 9.4. Registry

Registry catalogs/looks up identified documentary entities or editions under declared provenance and freshness/current-historical-snapshot context. It does not redefine identity. A document lookup needs its domain/canonical key; an exact-edition lookup additionally needs edition/context evidence. No universal Registry intermediary, implemented resolver or persistent content availability is implied.

## 9.5. Relationships

Relationships owns typed connection records and provenance; Document Identity owns the contract for document endpoints. Other endpoint kinds use their own qualified identity domains. Canonical document reference validity requires the intended document/edition context and actual evidence; logical reference preservation does not imply live-content retrieval. Required edges remain required even when their data comes through a projection; a reference label cannot conceal a genuine cycle.

## 9.6. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph projects identified entities and Relationships records with source/edition provenance and refresh limits. Document nodes use document identity; graph edges or non-document entities need appropriate other contracts. Projections do not create competing identity/relationship authority or certify complete network correctness. No Registry→Graph→Baseline execution chain is prescribed.

## 9.7. Governance

Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines define documentary transition, decision, review and snapshot requirements; actual operation remains with DMS/tool/manual processes and CMS change scope. Identity-record lifecycle, document Status/Version/Revision, maturity, review, validation, approval, publication and membership are distinct. A state list alone is neither a universal permission graph nor an implemented workflow.

Baselines selects an explicitly identified immutable set of exact approved document editions with relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Identity alone cannot select an exact member; eligibility, consistency and actual inclusion remain separate checks. Draft successors neither inherit membership nor retarget older snapshots. Retired identities preserve reservations/history without implying current document publication or resolver availability.

## 4.2. Identifier



### 4.2.1. Purpose

Identifier is the canonical representation of assigned identity under its governing domain/canonicalization rules. The logical document, qualified key, rendered string and any permitted alias are distinct. Alternative representations must identify the intended existing key; they do not license another document to reuse it.

For this corpus, the domain is **Documentation Framework**, represented by **DF**. The adopted identifier convention is **DF-SSS-NNN**, where SSS is a registered uppercase three-letter stable allocation series and NNN is a positive three-digit allocation001–999. Full qualified identifiers, not numeric suffixes alone, determine collisions. The series records its allocation origin; current Family, Type, Component, path, Version/Revision and Status do not regenerate an assigned ID.

000 is not allocated and is not a README code. Gaps do not prove availability; allocated and retired numbers remain reserved. Allocation requires explicit series records and checks of relevant current/historical/reserved identities and references. At999, register an unused three-letter continuation series with traceability; do not widen syntax or recycle silently. Policy§4 and DID-001/003/004 establish these corpus rules. This schema integrates their scoped representation; other domains require explicit rules and no new allocation or migration occurs here.

Canonical interpretation states the responsible domain/rules and intended existing target. Alias/canonicalization handling must be explicit and preserve historical interpretation. Neither this format nor a syntax match proves allocation, uniqueness, a running resolver or retrieval availability.

---

### 4.2.2. Cardinality

```text
Exactly one
```

One canonical identifier representation per applicable assigned identity. Domain qualification remains required. Multiple aliases or physical representations do not create multiple logical document identities or erase the canonical interpretation requirement.

---

### 4.2.3. Characteristics

- **Mandatory:** a canonical identifier represents the applicable assigned identity.
- **Unique:** the qualified Domain+Identifier shall identify the intended document; actual collision/reservation coverage is recorded separately.
- **Immutable:** ordinary content/classification/status/edition/repository changes preserve the assigned key under its governing contract.
- **Permanent:** preserve same-document association and allocated/retired reservations; never reassign to another document.

Deterministic interpretation is a governed representation requirement, not proof of an implemented generator/resolver. Necessary contract/migration changes require the prior/new assessment in §11 rather than silent reallocation.

---

# 6. Logical Relationships

The second view preserves the same three subjects as the received relationship diagram. It qualifies direction, authority and subject; it is not a mandatory object layout, operational call chain or required-dependency graph.

| Assigned Document Identity | is represented through | Identifier | One canonical interpretation under domain rules |

<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Minimal key/association scope is distinct from the complete subject claimed by other specifications. The following records actual peer requirements; it neither deletes mandatory peer fields nor invents an accepted merged record/state machine.

| Domain / Identifier | Assigned governing qualification and canonical representation | DID-003 §§4–6; DID-004 §§4/7; DID-014 §§7–8 mandatory Domain/Identifier | Preserve qualified key and explicitly governed corpus representation/other domains |

| Identity State / Lifecycle State | Not introduced as a merged key field by this source | DID-014 §§7–8 mandates State/Lifecycle State; DID-006 §§4–8 defines Unassigned/Assigned/Preserved/Retired for its lifecycle subject | Reconcile field/record subject,authority,vocabulary and transitions with owners; no implicit removal or universal-state approval |

DID-004 retains Active/Archived/Deprecated as historical candidate terminology; these are not automatically equivalent to DID-006 lifecycle states or document-edition Draft/Review/Approved/Published/Archived status. Unassigned concerns pre-allocation, not an already assigned key. State,Status,exact edition,maturity,approval and Baseline membership require their proper subject/owner evidence. Contradictory complete-record claims require a coordinated owner decision before claiming a fully reconciled implementation contract.

# 8. Schema Constraints

The following requirements concern the stated assigned key and incoming-association subjects. Requirement text is not execution evidence. Record responsible contracts/editions,artifacts/domain/context,executor,coverage,observations and unresolved conditions for any claimed check.

---

## 8.1. Identity Domain

- A governing domain shall qualify every applicable assigned key; pre-allocation subjects and excluded functional files differ.
- Ordinary evolution preserves the assigned domain/key association under its governing contract.
- Domain qualification,owner,rules and namespace/collision/reservation coverage shall be explicit; a domain declaration does not prove actual uniqueness.
- A necessary migration affecting the governing contract requires §11 prior/new reconciliation and continuity checks before application; no silent domain reassignment is authorized.

---

## 8.2. Identifier

- Each applicable assigned identity has one canonical identifier representation under its domain rules.
- Full qualified key uniqueness requires actual allocation/collision/reservation evidence; matching syntax alone does not prove it.

- Allocated and retired identifiers shall never be reassigned to another document. Preserve old representations,reservations and historical references/snapshot selections through any necessary governed transition.
- Apply §4.2 corpus syntax and canonicalization scope; no new series,identifier,alias or migration is created by this UPDATE.

---

## 8.3. Identity References

- A valid document-targeting reference identifies its intended existing qualified document or exact edition/context; other endpoint kinds follow their own contracts.
- Incoming population remains optional0..N; an identity does not need an incoming reference merely to exist.
- References never allocate or redefine their target and remain external to the identifier.
- Connection records retain their relationship owner and provenance; mutations do not automatically change the target key.
- Record dangling,ambiguous,stale or unavailable references as actual observations; preserve historical interpretation and never silently retarget. Identity stability alone guarantees no live-content retrieval or universal future reference validity.

---

# 11. Extensibility

Schema evolution shall preserve same-document assignment,non-reuse and compatible meaning where feasible. Additional roles may be introduced only through an explicit responsible contract and impact assessment,not by treating a picture or Metadata representation as an automatically registered field.

Before a necessary normative change or path/identity migration:

2. Assess compatibility,mandatory-field/State/Canonical Reference effects,record populations,canonical representation/aliases and reference targets; retain unresolved peer claims visibly.
3. Record exact old→new mappings,collision/reservation/history checks,same-document continuity and relevant exact-edition/snapshot contexts. Preserve old evidence and never retarget immutable historical snapshot members or reassign retired IDs.
4. Establish transition verification and coordinated propagation before claiming integrated conformance. A local source update does not approve peers or execute migration.

For changed working document editions,compatible correction retains Version,compatible additive capability increments minor,incompatible contract change increments major and resets minor to0. Each persisted changed edition increments Revision monotonically across Versions. Unchanged-source validation changes neither coordinate and is recorded centrally. Those documentary coordinates do not define all other entities' allocation/lifecycle.

DID-014 §14's received additive/backward-compatible-only extension rule remains a real peer contract requiring scheduled reconciliation with the controlled-evolution approach;it is not silently waived by this source. No blanket permission to mutate assigned identity is introduced. This UPDATE executes no allocation,series registration,alias or migration.

## 5.2. Classification

Classification owns category meaning, distinct from the key of a classified normalized document.

---

### 5.2.1. Dependency

Classification→Document Identity is the required document-identification contract for an applicable assigned normalized document receiving classification. It is not a requirement that each category/definition/assignment entity has a DF document key.

### 5.2.2. Purpose

Classification categorizes the intended document under its own contracts. Family/Type/Component changes do not regenerate the stable allocated series/key. A category entity's identity and a normalized document describing that category are different subjects. Classification does not redefine document-key meaning.

# 7. Relationships with Discovery Components

The five original Discovery responsibilities remain separate from identity allocation and actual runtime delivery. Logical contracts may constrain projections and interfaces; actual availability, freshness and results need observations.

---

## 7.1. Registry

Registry→Document Identity is the required identification contract for document registrations. Registry owns registration/index records; Document Identity owns the underlying document-key meaning. Registry→Metadata is a selected descriptor contract in ARC-005§12. Repeated records/copies do not alone prove duplicate allocation. Record exact source editions, intended target/context, provenance and freshness. Registration is not allocation, approval or a mandatory intermediary for every consumer.

---

## 7.2. Relationships

Relationships owns connection type, direction, endpoints and connection records. For a document endpoint use the intended qualified document or exact edition/context under §4.4; other typed endpoints follow their own contracts. No rule here forces all possible associations to be document-to-document. Mutable connections do not redefine the key, and canonical endpoints alone do not prove a valid connection or permanently available target.

---

## 7.3. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph owns logical node/edge projection and representation contracts; storage/runtime technologies remain implementation choices. Knowledge Graph→Document Identity for document-node meaning and Knowledge Graph→Relationships for typed connections are selected required contracts in ARC-005§12. Neither is eliminated by calling the graph a projection.

Keep authoritative keys/connection sources distinct from projected records/properties. Nodes and properties may change while preserving intended qualified identity. Retain source edition/context, derivation, provenance, freshness and observed limitations. Projection does not allocate a new document identity, acquire connection authority or prove every peer representation is synchronized.

---

## 7.4. Navigation

Navigation uses intended identity and context to locate an applicable document or edition under its navigation contract. It can derive links and presentation records while preserving authoritative target meaning; the received prohibition on creating identity information means no competing allocation/semantic invention, not a ban on derived representation. Navigation does not guarantee successful current retrieval, require a universal Registry route or authorize silent retargeting.

---

## 7.5. Search

Search→Document Identity is the required identification contract for document-targeting search results. Other indexed entities retain their own endpoint contracts. Search owns query/result behavior, not document-key meaning. Record actual indexed source editions/context, target interpretation, freshness and result/retrieval observations. An index match does not prove allocation, complete population coverage, full identity validity or future availability.
