## 2. Applicability and boundaries

This Model applies to the semantic organization of the actual intended documentary subjects in their declared scheme and rule context. Its normalized-document Family/Type/Class rules apply to normalized documents under the current working corpus convention. Every file named README.md, CHANGELOG.md or ArchitecturalMilestones.md, at any location, remains a non-normalized functional file; this Model does not mandate normalized fields or allocate identities to those files. They remain subject to applicable content, reference, evidence and consistency checks.

A logical document, a particular document edition, a classification definition, a semantic value, an assignment and a representation of that assignment are distinct subjects. A pre-allocation draft can be discussed without pretending it already has an assigned document key. A diagram, example or descriptor field does not establish that an assignment actually occurred. Applicable owner rules govern whether a draft may receive a classification and what subject evidence is required.

This Model defines conceptual meaning and local working invariants. It does not prescribe a database schema, serialization language, mandatory physical record, executable classifier, complete vocabulary population, general cardinality catalog, lifecycle engine, permission system or implemented integration. Detailed structural, lifecycle, validation, governance, relationship and extension rules retain their responsible sources. Missing or conflicting mandatory owner evidence prevents a broad conformance claim; it is not silently filled by a diagram or treated as an observed violation.

## 6. Scheme and context

A scheme identifies how its semantic options are defined and interpreted. The governing context supplies the distinctions needed by the actual claim: which scheme and definition sources apply, which edition or effective conditions are intended, and any relevant domain, time or usage scope. The required context is claim-dependent. This is not a new universally mandatory list of physical fields or an authorization mechanism.

The same textual label in different schemes or source editions does not prove the same category, value or meaning. Conversely, two representations can express the same governed semantic option when an actual definition/mapping establishes that equivalence. Interpretation requires the applicable definitions and authority, not string equality alone.

A scheme's documented availability is not evidence that all possible options are populated, approved or currently assignable. Actual scheme membership, definition edition and lifecycle/usage rules must be checked where material. This Model does not fill an unavailable Class vocabulary or invent categories from illustrative placeholders.

## 7. Classification Element as a dimension

An Element is the conceptual role in which a classification distinction is expressed. For normalized documents, Family identifies actual component/admitted documentary-area membership, Type identifies primary documentary responsibility and Class can express an additional defined non-conflicting distinction. A role's meaning and the value represented in that role are separate.

Received Elements §36 calls its Family/Type/Class view a complete conceptual element model, while its §§6–7 preserve earlier role meanings. That is actual received peer evidence, not proof that the current role/category/assignment distinctions and every cardinality are integrated. Family, Type and Class here are neither three automatically created Metadata Elements nor three architectural components.

Other dimensions require explicit responsible definitions, applicability, relationships and compatible or justified incompatible change assessment. A new dimension does not extend the permitted Type enumeration or waive mandatory existing rules. Naming and population belong to actual definition owners; this Model does not allocate their identifiers.

## 8. Category and definition

A Category is a defined semantic option within its actual scheme/context. Its identity, definition, label, lifecycle assertion and usage are separate concerns. A definition states the option's governed meaning and scope; a readable label represents that meaning in a context and need not be its identity.

Definition evidence must be adequate for the actual interpretation claim. A category placeholder, a title in a catalog or an unqualified term is not automatically an admitted category. When a definition changes, preserve the exact prior meaning/source edition and determine whether the current change is a compatible clarification, an additive capability or an incompatible semantic revision. Neither historical interpretation nor present assignment permission follows from a label remaining unchanged.

This working distinction supports source-qualified category relationships and usage evidence without prescribing a universal category object structure, globally unique category-ID syntax or normative population of all schemes. Those require their responsible definition/schema/constraint decisions.

## 9. Value, representation and interpretation

A Value expresses a classification meaning in an Element role under an applicable context. A representation such as the string `Architecture` is interpreted as the current Type responsibility only when the governing role/context establishes that meaning. The same word in a title, directory or historical citation is not necessarily a current Type assignment.

A value may select a governed category; that relationship is not assumed to be universal one-to-one. Actual scheme/schema definitions decide whether alternate representations, combinations or additional semantic relationships are permitted. Identity, synonymy, formatting, label equivalence and semantic compatibility require their actual rules and evidence.

Representations in a Markdown header, Metadata Instance, template output, index or graph projection do not acquire authority to redefine Classification. A correction to rendering must be distinguished from a correction to assignment meaning. Meaning changes require responsible owner/consumer and compatibility assessment even when the lexical value is unchanged.

## 10. Assignment and membership

An Assignment is an actual governed association concerning an intended document and an interpreted value/category under its Element role and applicable context. For an assigned normalized document, the governing qualified document key identifies the logical subject. An edition-specific assertion also identifies the intended edition/bytes/context. Pre-allocation claims must identify their real temporary subject and limitations without inventing an assigned K.

Evidence for an actual assignment must establish the intended subject, the represented role/value and governing definition/rules/source editions, together with the authority, usage/time or decision context required by the claim. These are semantic evidence obligations, not a prescribed universal persisted tuple. The mere presence of a classification definition, a label in an example or a validation log does not establish that the association was authorized or performed.

Membership is the semantic consequence of an actual valid applicable assignment. A category's member list is not physical containment or evidence of complete population coverage. Current membership and current permission to create another assignment may differ from preserved historical membership under an earlier definition. Actual applicability and responsible rules decide the claim.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  D["Intended document / selected edition"] -->|subject of evidence| A["Actual assignment claim"]
  R["Role, value and governing definition context"] -->|interprets| A
  U["Applicable authority and usage rules"] -->|constrains| A
  A -->|supports when valid for the claim| M["Semantic membership"]
```

This newly authored view represents evidence and semantics. It neither performs an assignment nor equates evaluation, authorization and historical interpretation.

## 11. Family

For an applicable normalized document, Family identifies the actual canonical component or explicitly admitted non-component documentary area under current common Architecture and Review Policy §3. Component documents use the canonical name of their component; when Component is present it matches that actual membership. Current component names include Metadata, Document Identity, Classification and Templates. `DocumentIdentity` is a directory spelling, not a separate canonical component.

Foundation, Architecture and global Roadmap are admitted non-component documentary areas in their actual policy scope. The framework container is not its own component. Component roadmaps use the Family of the component they plan even when physically stored under Roadmaps. A path or allocation-series prefix does not determine Family.

Earlier broad-domain Family definitions remain exact historical or pending peer evidence. They are not an alternative simultaneous governing rule for this current normalized-document operation. This Model establishes no universal category cardinality for every other scheme or arbitrary entity from this corpus rule.

## 12. Type

Type identifies exactly one primary documentary responsibility for each applicable normalized document. Its meaning is uniform across Families.

| Type | Primary responsibility |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Foundations, principles, concepts, conceptual models/elements and architectural decisions |
| Structure | Organization, composition, schemas, structural relationships, restrictions and element catalogs |
| Behavior | Processes, lifecycle, validation, governance, extensibility and planned evolution |
| Reference | Consultation, terminology, consolidated specifications, examples, recommendations and historical records |

Use the spelling Behavior. Concepts, Model, Elements, Schema, Dictionary, Lifecycle, Base and Core are not extra Type values merely because they occur in titles or directories. Content and primary responsibility determine Type. Historical consultation is Reference; a process or planned evolution is Behavior. An applicable mixed-content document still identifies its actual primary responsibility.

Family does not create a separate Type vocabulary or redefine a Type's responsibility. Actual contextual applicability constraints may limit a particular use without redefining the meaning of the four Type values. Type=Reference alone neither grants nor removes normative authority, formal approval or publication status.

## 13. Class

Class is a separate optional semantic dimension. Its use requires an explicit definition and applicability that does not conflict with the governing Family/Type meanings or merely duplicate Type without an actual additional distinction. Absence of Class is not a defect solely because a received conceptual tuple lists it.

This Model does not establish a complete Class enumeration, universal Type→Class hierarchy, mandatory Class value or physical field. If the actual context needs a Class vocabulary or permitted combinations, the responsible definition/schema/constraint decisions must specify them with evidence. Optional does not mean an unrestricted string or a fifth Type.

Current Concepts §14 preserves the received nature/role subject but qualifies its present interpretation. Actual unchanged peers that place Class under Type remain pending source-qualified reconciliation. Neither an illustrative diagram nor this acknowledgment approves those relationships for every current assignment.

## 15. Semantic relationships and hierarchies

Relationships within Classification have actual semantic endpoint kinds and direction. Role/value interpretation, category membership, category specialization, documentary assignment, label equivalence, supersession and deprecation are different relations. Their names or arrows are not interchangeable evidence of the same constraint.

The current normalized-document Family and Type dimensions do not form the earlier universal specialization hierarchy. Class is not universally subordinate to Type. Actual category schemes can define hierarchical or non-hierarchical relations when their responsible definitions, scope and constraints do so. There is no prohibition on every hierarchy merely because the old Family-dependent Type hierarchy is replaced.

Acyclicity applies only where the actual relation/schema rules require it. Received Relationships §43 explicitly qualifies invalid cycles by relationship type and applicable Schema. It is not proof that all semantic graphs, general Relationships, navigation or required-service dependencies are one DAG. Source/target meaning, inverse, symmetry and transitivity require their own rules; they do not follow from arrow appearance.

Where the general Relationships component records a connection, it owns connection/endpoints/provenance contracts; Classification owns the classification meaning of the connection. Projection into a Knowledge Graph cannot redefine either authority. No connection record or graph node is created by publishing this conceptual view.

## 17. Labels, aliases and historical interpretation

A label can change without changing category identity when the responsible definition permits it; a semantic change can occur while a label stays unchanged. An alias or synonym needs actual scoped equivalence evidence and source/edition applicability. A textual resemblance or matching numeric suffix is not sufficient.

Historical labels and examples retain their original interpretation context. They must not silently resolve to another category, document or edition following a current correction. A current reference can target a logical document or an explicitly pinned edition; a pinned historical member retains its original bytes/context even when a later working successor exists.

The wrong received CLS001 header at this path is not legitimized as a semantic or documentary alias. History records the error and localized correction. Actual external integrations, consumers or caches with ambiguous unqualified CLS001 references require intended-target investigation; a global substitution would corrupt genuine Architecture references. Current operational ambiguity must be resolved before those consumers are claimed integrated.

## 18. Definition editions, usage and physical independence

A definition edition identifies the governed interpretation used by the actual assignment claim. It is not automatically the governing document's Version coordinate or a new universal record type. Applicable sources must establish the real linkage where documentary editions carry definition meaning.

Preserving an assignment's historical meaning does not automatically authorize its present use. Deprecated/retired definition evidence, current assignment permission, current membership, historical membership, reference validity and observed live retrieval are separate questions. Repositories, Registry entries, graph projections and Metadata representations may become stale while historical intended meaning remains interpretable.

Moving a file does not by itself change category identity, assigned document K or semantic membership. It can affect references, representations, indexes, adapter interfaces or access. Those actual effects require their responsible checks. Technology/format/storage independence preserves semantic ownership; it is not evidence that every representation or provider contract is unaffected by a physical change.

## 19. Metadata projection and ownership

Classification owns the meaning of its categories, roles, interpreted values, assignments and applicable classification conditions. Metadata owns descriptive element definitions and its Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance contracts. Representation of classification in Metadata does not transfer semantic authority to Metadata, Templates, Registry or a header parser.

For an actual applicable Metadata Instance, its governing effective Profile must be identified under the responsible Metadata contract. This Model creates neither a complete Profile nor a Classification field catalog. Family, Type, Class, scheme/context or assignment evidence here is conceptual meaning; it is not proof that corresponding Metadata Elements have canonical identifiers, complete descriptor schemas or publication/lifecycle records.

An actual projection needs intended semantic subject, source definition/rules/edition, representation mapping, applicable descriptor/profile/interface, cardinality/omission handling, provenance and checks required by that claim. Compatible rendering and semantic correction are assessed separately. An indispensable governed representation creates an actual Classification→Metadata requirement in that scope; calling it a projection does not remove the required provider.

## 20. Document Identity interfaces

Classification consumes Document Identity when an applicable assigned normalized-document subject or document endpoint must be identified. A logical-document claim uses its governing K; an exact-edition claim adds the actual edition/bytes/context. A category's identity and the key of a document describing that category remain distinct.

Current DID014 V2.0 R1 makes a local working distinction between K and complete supporting assigned record R. Complete R retains five mandatory roles: Document Identity, Identifier, Identity Domain, Identity State and Canonical Reference. Identity State/Lifecycle State is a scoped R assertion, not document Status or generic Metadata State. Canonical Reference is the intended qualified canonical target/edition descriptor, not a required incoming Relationships edge or a promise of live retrieval. K-only evidence is not full R conformity.

That exact DID specification decision is not globally accepted or fully propagated field/interface agreement. Current DID005/003/004/006/013 meanings and DF-DID-005 §11, DF-DID-010 §12, DF-DID-011 §§4.2/9 and DF-DID-013 §9 earlier-restriction references retain actual source-specific reconciliation limits. This Model consumes the needed meaning without claiming complete merged DID/Metadata schemas or silently changing those sources.

## 21. Templates, Governance and other consumers

Templates owns reusable structural definitions and applicable instance contracts. When a Classification representation actually requires a Template contract, identify that conditional Classification→Templates interface; not every assignment requires Templates. A template may expose governed fields but cannot redefine category meaning or manufacture an assignment merely by including a placeholder.

Classification owns its domain-specific conditions, definition changes and assignment semantics. Common Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines retain governance contracts; actual management/approval/publication or permission execution belongs to the authorized executor and applicable DMS/tool/manual process. A CMS may manage the actual change process. This Model neither implements those systems nor transfers owner responsibility through a diagram.

Discovery consumes semantic information for organization, navigation and search. Registry catalogs registrations/index records with source/freshness evidence; it does not create entity existence or allocate document identity. Relationships records governed connections and endpoints; Knowledge Graph projects actual authoritative subjects/connections. Automation capabilities and Integration adapters need actual inputs, outputs, mapping, authorization and checks. Semantic support is not blanket permission to create, migrate, publish or retire anything.

## 23. Lifecycle boundaries

Definition lifecycle and documentary usage are separate subjects. Actual CLS006 §20 proposes Defined, Active, Deprecated and Retired for classification definitions; its §§7–8 distinguishes definition lifecycle from usage. This Model preserves those source roles and does not promote a proposal to approved/implemented state machinery. The word introduced can describe an action without being a canonical state or automatic alias for Defined.

Document Status, definition lifecycle, assignment usage/current permission, identity R state assertion, review-finding state and Milestone state are distinct. No shared word makes them aliases. State/transition applicability requires actual intended subject, event/rule, authority, decision and evidence under the responsible owner contract.

Deprecation can preserve historical meaning while discouraging or restricting new usage under actual rules. It does not automatically warn, invalidate, migrate or erase every prior assignment. Retirement similarly does not silently retarget pinned definitions or document editions. Actual usage decisions and transition evidence must be preserved separately from historical interpretation.

## 24. Validation and result semantics

A Model claim identifies intended subject/population, semantic/representation/interface scope, exact source editions/artifacts/bytes/context, applicable responsible rules, authority/executor, performed and unperformed checks, observations, coverage and limits. Validation compares actual observations with applicable rules and is nonmutating; correction, assignment, permission, acceptance and formal approval require their own authorization/evidence.

Actual CLS007 §§39–42 provides Valid, Valid with Warnings and Invalid. Valid with Warnings requires no blocking rule violation and actual non-blocking findings; deprecated usage is not automatically a warning or universally invalid. Invalid requires an actual applicable blocking violation. Rule-dependent outcome meaning is not replaced by an imported DID outcome vocabulary or a selected binary diagram.

Missing, unperformed or conflicting mandatory evidence withholds a broader success claim without fabricating an observed blocking violation. Incomplete assessment and an actual invalid assignment are different conclusions. Narrow documentary checks can succeed while Model implementation, authoritative category population, full Schema/Constraints compliance or global owner integration remains unestablished.

No classification assignment, lifecycle transition or source correction is performed by a validation result. Result recording and reproducible evidence retain their actual executor and date; changing a source after a completed check requires an appropriate successor and later check rather than extending an earlier PASS to new bytes.

## 25. Governance, change authority and traceability

A proposed classification definition, association or rule change identifies its actual owner, need, rationale, alternatives, prior/new meaning, consumers, applicable authority, compatibility and transition. Actual decisions and implemented effects are recorded separately. A review command authorizes its declared documentary operation; it does not approve an architecture globally or grant operational permissions by implication.

Maintain traceability between semantic definitions, applicable source editions, intended documentary subjects, actual assignments, descriptor projections, relationship endpoints, decisions and later checks where relevant to the claim. A complete traceability claim requires actual population/coverage evidence; this conceptual list is not proof that all connections exist.

No component may silently redefine another owner's responsibility. Common Governance contracts and an actual CMS/DMS/tool/manual executor retain their own scope. This Model creates no lifecycle record, publication state, Baseline membership, category allocation or mandatory all-term consultation rule merely by listing those subjects.

## 26. Evolution and compatibility

Ordinary compatible evolution preserves applicable definitions, assigned same-document continuity and historical interpretation where feasible. Necessary assessed normative/foundational/responsibility/interface/domain revision is permitted under actual common Architecture AP-015–018 and responsible change authority; it is not automatically compatible because it is called an extension.

The received Architecture copy's §§28/31.4/35 asserted evolution without changing foundations, preservation of existing semantic meaning and unqualified architectural compatibility. Those exact previous clauses remain in the old body/view/map evidence. They are not simultaneous current rules in this reconstructed Model. Current genuine Architecture §28 explicitly replaces those absolute restrictions with ordinary preservation versus necessary assessed revision.

A necessary revision must preserve actual prior artifacts/failed checks and identify old/new rules, subject/domain/context, need, alternatives, rationale, responsible authority, owners, consumers and indispensable interfaces. Assess old→new definition/category/value/alias/assignment/reference mappings, key/domain/collision/reservation history and exact snapshot continuity. Resolve actual reciprocal requirements and transition effects rather than conceal them with relation names. Apply only the authorized scoped change with actual contributor/history evidence and later checks.

Under the working Review Policy, compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract/convention change increments major and resets minor to0. Revision increments monotonically across Version changes. Unchanged-source validation increments neither. Real compatibility depends on permitted meaning and interfaces, not a filename correction or number alone. No arbitrary semantic mutation, allocated/retired key reuse, silent historical retargeting or automatic assignment migration follows from this evolution rule.

# 34. Schema Cardinality

This working structural matrix separates already justified normalized-role obligations from unestablished general multiplicities and representation decisions. It replaces the received blanket deferral of every optionality/cardinality question; it does not invent complete authoritative counts.

# 49. Cross-Component Relationships

Classification Relationships may have implications outside the Classification component.

For example:

```text

            Classification
            │
            ├── Registry
            ├── Discovery
            ├── Knowledge Graph
            ├── Metadata
            └── Automation

```

These components may consume Classification relationships.

However, their internal relationship models remain outside the scope of this document.

---

# 50. Relationship and Metadata

Classification and Metadata are related but distinct concepts.

Classification Relationships describe relationships between Classification Elements.

Metadata relationships describe relationships involving Metadata Elements.

The two models may interact, but one does not replace the other.

---

# 51. Relationship and Document Identity

Classification Relationships do not define Document Identity relationships.

A document may be classified using a Classification Element:

```text

                 Document
                    │
              classified as
                    │
                    ▼

          Classification Element

```

The relationship between a Document and a Classification Element belongs to the document classification mechanism.

The relationships defined in this document primarily concern Classification Elements themselves.

---

# 52. Relationship and Registry

The Registry may expose Classification Relationships for discovery.

However:

```text

            Classification Relationships
            │
            └── defines semantic relationship

            Registry
            │
            └── exposes registered relationship information

```

The Registry does not redefine Classification semantics.

---

# 53. Relationship and Knowledge Graph

Classification Relationships may become edges in a Knowledge Graph.

Conceptually:

```text

          Classification Element
                    │
               relationship
                    │
                    ▼

          Classification Element

```

may be represented as:

```text

            Node  ─────  Edge  ─────►  Node

```

The Knowledge Graph is an external representation and discovery mechanism.

The Classification Relationship remains the authoritative semantic definition.

---

# 61. Relationship Historical Preservation

Historical relationships should remain interpretable.

When a relationship is deprecated or retired, its historical meaning should remain available where necessary.

For example:

```text

                Old Class
                    │
               replaced by
                    │
                    ▼

                New Class

```

preserves the evolution of the Classification model.

---

# 63. Relationship Impact

Relationship changes may have local or cross-component impact.

Examples:

| Change | Potential Impact |
|--------|------------------|
| New relationship | Local / Dictionary / Validation |
| Changed cardinality | Schema / Validation |
| Changed relationship semantics | Entire Classification architecture |
| Deprecated relationship | Existing Classification |
| Retired relationship | Historical data |
| New inverse | Navigation / Discovery |
| New cross-component relationship | Registry / Knowledge Graph |

Impact shall be evaluated before approval.

---

# 13. Classification Hierarchy

The primary hierarchy can therefore be represented as:

```text

            Family
            │
            ├── Type
            │   ├── Class
            │   ├── Class
            │   └── Class
            │
            ├── Type
            │   ├── Class
            │   └── Class
            │
            └── Type

```

This hierarchy provides the structural organization of Classification.

---

# 20. Relationship Cardinality

A Classification Relationship may impose cardinality constraints.

For example:

```text

            Family 1  ─────  * Type
            Type   1  ─────  * Class

```

This represents the conceptual model in which:

- a Family may contain multiple Types;
- a Type belongs to a Family;
- a Type may contain multiple Classes;
- a Class belongs to a Type.

The exact cardinality constraints are subject to the Classification Schema and Classification Specification.

---

# 43. Acyclicity

Hierarchical Classification relationships should preserve an acyclic structure.

For example:

```text

                  Family
                    │
                    ▼

                   Type
                    │
                    ▼

                  Class

```

must not result in:

```text

                  Family
                    │
                    ▼

                   Type
                    │
                    ▼

                  Class
                  │
                  └────────► Family

```

when the relationship type is hierarchical and acyclic.

Cycles shall be treated as invalid where prohibited by the Classification Schema.

---

# 1. Introduction

This document defines a bounded working lifecycle contract for Classification definitions and their governed evolution. It uses current Architecture DF-CLS-001, Concepts DF-CLS-002, reconstructed Model DF-CLS-003, Elements DF-CLS-004 and Schema DF-CLS-005, all V2.0 R1, with their actual source-local authority and remaining integration limits. The Model is explicitly reconstructed, not recovered authentic historical text or globally accepted architecture. Elements' known Type Architecture/02-Structure placement remains unmet M13 work; Schema's local validation does not resolve it.

The three original documentary role subjects remain:

- Family;
- Type;
- Class.

Current Family means actual component/admitted documentary-area membership; Type is exactly one uniform primary responsibility; Class is optional, explicitly defined and non-conflicting. A governing role definition, admitted category/value definition, actual assignment and descriptor representation are distinct subjects. Defining or retiring an option does not silently revise a mandatory role contract.

This lifecycle concerns definition evolution, not the lifecycle of every document, file or runtime object. Document Version, Revision and Status remain distinct; Metadata grouping is a descriptive projection rather than transfer of domain ownership or proof of a complete field catalog. No transition, assignment, permission, approval or migration is performed by publishing this working text.

---

# 4. Classification Lifecycle Concept

A Classification definition supplies governed semantic meaning for an identified role, category/value option, relationship or schema condition in its actual scope. Definition identity, wording/edition, interpreted value, readable label, actual assignment and descriptor field are not interchangeable or universally one-to-one.

The received Family=META and Type=DCL examples are historical codes from earlier documentation, not current canonical Family/Type values or evidence of assignments. Definition/Active Use/Deprecation/Retirement in the received view are concerns/actions, not automatically registered aliases for Defined/Active/Deprecated/Retired.

The received assertion that no normative state vocabulary is established remains prior evidence. Supplied Governance, Constraints, Dictionary and Specification actually contain lifecycle terms and mandatory conditions (§56). This working edition states the bounded four-state interpretation in §20 and transition/authority limits in §48, without promoting a proposal to approved architecture or pretending all exact guards and routes are supplied.

# 6. Classification Definitions

Actual Dictionary §§6.1/6.5–6.7 uses broader Element/Category/Value/Assignment language; §§9.1/11 defines Element-based lifecycle terms. Those differences remain mapped, not declared a completed canonical merger.

The lifecycle assertion concerns the identified definition and its actual edition/context, not every document using it. General populations, one-to-one definition/value cardinality, mandatory context fields and a complete event record are not invented here. # 7. Lifecycle Subject

The lifecycle subject is the actual identified Classification definition in its governing role/category/value/relationship/schema scope and definition edition/context. It is not automatically the documentary file, every current assignment, a Metadata artifact or a universal runtime object.

A document can retain the same logical identity while a referenced definition changes state. Whether an existing assignment remains historically valid, whether current use is admitted and whether a target is retrievable are separate evidenced claims. Definition-state changes alone neither rewrite assignment history nor alter documentary Status or permission.

# 8. Lifecycle Dimensions

# 1. Introduction

This document defines a bounded working contract for evaluating actual Classification claims against applicable responsible-owner rules. It uses current Architecture DF-CLS-001, Concepts DF-CLS-002, reconstructed Model DF-CLS-003, Elements DF-CLS-004, Schema DF-CLS-005 and Lifecycle DF-CLS-006, all V2.0 R1, with their actual source-local authority and remaining integration limits. The Model is explicitly reconstructed, not recovered authentic historical text or globally accepted architecture. Elements' known Type Architecture/02-Structure placement remains unmet M13 work.

The three original documentary role subjects remain:

- Family;
- Type;
- Class.

Current Family is actual component/admitted-area membership; Type is exactly one uniform primary responsibility; Class is optional, explicitly defined and non-conflicting. Governing role, category/value interpretation, definition/source edition, actual assignment, documentary claim and descriptor representation differ.

Classification owns its semantic and domain evaluation conditions. Validation consumes actual rules without redefining them, mutating its subject or approving architecture. This source neither implements a checker nor performs an assignment, transition, permission, migration, publication or Baseline selection. A result identifies actual subject, rules, authority, evidence, coverage and limits rather than treating source presence or selected checks as complete implementation success.

---

# 6. Validation Subject

The validation subject is the actual declared Classification structure, interpreted role/value/category, definition/state claim, documentary assignment or descriptor representation within its responsible scope. The generic received Classification Instance label is not a universal mandatory three-field physical object, complete category population or evidence that an association was performed.

Identify governing role and any admitted category/value definition, readable label, definition/source edition, actual intended logical-document or explicitly selected exact-edition assignment, rule/context and evidence. These are not universally one-to-one subjects. Actual Dictionary broader Element/Category/Value/Assignment uses remain mapped to current Model/Elements/Schema distinctions, not silently merged into a completed vocabulary.

Actual Schema, Dictionary, Lifecycle, Constraints and independently applicable Specification/Metadata/Profile/Identity clauses govern the claim. Source presence alone does not supply every mandatory rule, prove complete authority or establish an accepted architecture. Selected diagrams allocate no entities and perform no evaluation or assignment.

# 8. Validation Categories

The seven original complementary categories remain:

1. Structural Validation
2. Vocabulary Validation
3. Semantic Validation
4. Consistency Validation
5. Lifecycle Validation
6. Referential Validation
7. Architectural Validation

These are evaluation concerns, not new components, document Type values or an exhaustive execution schedule. The eight rule-category rows in §36 separately include Relationship as a rule concern. Coverage must map actual applicable rules to the claim rather than assume category names establish completeness.

Actual Metadata Validation§7 also has Profile Validation for descriptor representations. Classification domain checks do not waive an applicable Metadata Instance/effective-Profile requirement or transfer domain semantics to Metadata. Actual source editions and owner/interface authority remain explicit (§78).

# 11. Family Validation

Family means actual canonical component or admitted non-component documentary-area membership for the applicable normalized document. Component documents use their canonical component; Component, when present, matches membership. Foundation/Architecture/global Roadmap retain admitted non-component scope; the framework container is not a component of itself. Component roadmap storage, directory aliases and stable allocation series do not redefine Family.

An actual supplied value needs responsible definition/interpretation, admitted scope and evidence under applicable rules. Existence alone is a bounded condition, not complete assignment validity or permission. The META/broad-domain example is explicitly historical, not a current complete Family population or performed assignment. Received Valid/Invalid labels are selected conditional outcomes, not exhaustive current vocabulary or observed execution; actual §39 also retains Valid with Warnings and coverage limits.

# 12. Type Validation

Type is exactly one uniform primary documentary responsibility from Architecture, Structure, Behavior and Reference for every applicable normalized document. Actual primary content governs; title/filename alone does not assign Type or confer normative approval.

The three original checks remain with current interpretation:

- that the Type value is defined: one of the current responsibilities under its governing definition, not an invented Family-specific vocabulary;
- that it is valid in the applicable Family context: actual contextual usage restrictions can apply without redefining the uniform responsibility or making every pair automatically valid;
- that its semantic definition is preserved: evaluation consumes actual definitions/editions; a necessary governing revision needs separately assessed authority and history.

The received within-Family specialization/second-level definition and Family→Type view are historical meaning, not a simultaneous current rule. Actual known exactly-one obligation is not deferred until a complete vocabulary appears. Schema, Model, Elements and independent Constraints retain their real current/earlier differences and applicability.

# 13. Class Validation

Class is an optional additional explicitly defined non-conflicting distinction, separate from Type's primary responsibility. Any supplied value needs an actual responsible definition/scope and applicable use/structural rules even when no complete Class enumeration exists. Optional does not mean unrestricted or exempt from checking.

The received document-nature meaning is historical. No complete authoritative population, mandatory third value or physical field, universal child level, unrestricted string, fifth Type or unsupported maximum multiplicity is introduced. Current Schema§34 preserves genuine general-cardinality gaps without waiving known optionality and definition requirements.

| Applicable normalized Family | Actual canonical component/admitted documentary-area membership under adopted scope | Representation/profile and any further multiplicity need real rules; directory alias does not define membership |
| Applicable normalized Type | Exactly one primary value Architecture/Structure/Behavior/Reference, uniformly across Families | Actual context can restrict use without creating another Type vocabulary |
| Class | Optional; any supplied value needs explicit non-conflicting definition and applicable rules | No complete population, universal maximum or mandatory physical field established here |
| Category/value/assignment/relationship populations | Apply actual responsible definition, structure/use and endpoint rules to the intended claim | General counts, one-to-one mappings and complete populations remain unestablished unless actual authority supplies them |
| Descriptor/Profile representation | Apply actual Metadata Dictionary/Schema/effective Profile/Instance and interface requirements where applicable | Three role labels are not a complete physical record, canonical field catalog or serialization |
| Evaluation evidence | Identify actual applicable mandatory rules, observations and performed/unperformed coverage | Missing authority/checks withholds broad success; actual known violations are not erased or invented |

# 18. Unknown Values

A value unresolved against the actual applicable authoritative vocabulary is not semantically validated by that lookup. Distinguish an actual observed undefined-value violation under adequate governing authority from unresolved/absent/conflicting/incomplete source evidence. Missing lookup evidence alone does not manufacture a blocking violation or justify broad success.

The UNKNOWN example is an unallocated illustrative string. If actual rules and evidence establish that no corresponding admissible definition exists in the applicable scope, record the real observation and rule-dependent consequence; do not assume complete population merely from a file's presence.

The three original finding subjects remain:

- the affected element;
- the supplied value;
- the rule violated.

Where no actual violated rule is established, record the precise unresolved observation and evaluation limit rather than invent a violation. Intended subject, source/rule editions, applicability, authority and coverage remain traceable without defining a universal result-record schema.

# 17. Hierarchy Acyclicity

The Classification hierarchy shall not contain prohibited cycles.

For example, the following is invalid:

```text

                  Family
                    │
                    ▼

                   Type
                    │
                    ▼

                  Class
                  │
                  └────────► Family

```

when the relationships are hierarchical.

A hierarchical Classification structure must remain acyclic.

---

# 31. Lifecycle Constraints

Classification Lifecycle defines the states through which Classification Elements may evolve.

The conceptual lifecycle is:

```text

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

Classification Elements shall respect the rules applicable to their current lifecycle state.

---

# 32. Defined State

A Classification Element in the `Defined` state has been formally defined but is not necessarily available for normal active use.

It shall not be treated as Active unless the applicable lifecycle transition has occurred.

---

# 33. Active State

An Active Classification Element may be used according to its definition and applicable Classification rules.

Only valid and authorized Classification Elements may be Active.

---

# 34. Deprecated State

A Deprecated Classification Element shall not normally be used for new Classification assignments.

Existing historical uses may remain valid.

Deprecation shall preserve historical interpretation.

---

# 35. Retired State

A Retired Classification Element shall no longer be used as an active Classification Element.

Historical references may remain necessary for traceability.

Retirement shall not automatically imply deletion.

---

# 36. Lifecycle Transition Constraints

Classification Elements shall only undergo permitted lifecycle transitions.

For example:

```text

            Defined     ─────►  Active
            Active      ─────►  Deprecated
            Deprecated  ─────►  Retired

```

An invalid transition shall be rejected.

Governance authorizes lifecycle transitions.

Validation verifies that an observed lifecycle state conforms to the permitted lifecycle.

---

# 42. Non-Destructive Evolution

Classification evolution should prefer changes that preserve existing information.

For example:

```text

            Old Classification
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

               Replacement

```

is preferable to silently deleting the old Classification when historical traceability is required.

---

# 43. Migration Constraints

When Classification changes require migration, the migration shall preserve historical meaning.

A migration shall not silently convert historical Classification into a new semantic interpretation.

Where necessary, the original Classification shall remain traceable.

---

# 78. Relationship with Classification Lifecycle

Classification Lifecycle defines lifecycle states and transitions.

Classification Constraints defines restrictions applicable to those states and transitions.

Therefore:

```text

            Classification Lifecycle
            │
            └── defines lifecycle behavior

            Classification Constraints
            │
            └── constrains lifecycle behavior

```

---

# 46. Validation Responsibility

Classification Validation is responsible for identifying constraint violations.

It may determine that:

```text

                Constraint
                    │
                    ▼

          Satisfied / Violated

```

Validation does not modify the constraint.

---

# 53. Constraint Conflicts

Two constraints shall not establish contradictory requirements.

For example:

```text

    Constraint A:
    Type must belong to exactly one Family.

    Constraint B:
    Type may belong to multiple Families.

```

cannot both be canonical without an explicit contextual distinction.

Constraint conflicts must be resolved through Governance.

---

# 54. Constraint Precedence

Where multiple constraints apply, their relationship and precedence shall be explicitly defined by the Classification Specification.

An implementation shall not invent precedence rules when the canonical architecture does not define them.

---

# 56. Constraint Applicability

A constraint applies only when its applicability conditions are satisfied.

Conceptually:

```text

          Classification Element
                    │
                    ▼

              Applicability
              │
              ├── Not Applicable
              │
              └── Applicable
                      │
                      ▼

                  Evaluation

```

This prevents unrelated constraints from being applied universally.

---

# 58. Violation Identification

Constraint violation identification belongs to Classification Validation.

Conceptually:

```text

              Classification
                    │
                    ▼

          Constraint Evaluation
          │
          ├── Compliant
          │
          └── Violation
```

---

# 59. Violation Resolution

The resolution of architectural constraint violations belongs to Classification Governance where a governance decision is required.

For example:

```text

                Violation
                    │
                    ▼

          Governance Evaluation
          │
          ├── Correct
          ├── Accept temporarily
          ├── Deprecate
          └── Reject

```

Validation identifies.

Governance decides.

---

# 79. Relationship with Classification Validation

Classification Validation evaluates whether Classification satisfies the constraints.

Therefore:

```text

        Classification Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

        Classification Validation
                    │
                    ▼

            Conformance Result

```

Validation does not redefine the constraints.

---

# 45. Governance Constraint

Classification Constraints themselves shall evolve only through Classification Governance.

The relationship is:

```text

        Classification Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

        Classification Validation
        │
        └── detects violations

        Classification Governance
        │
        └── controls constraint evolution

```

This preserves the established separation between validation and governance. The analogous Metadata architecture explicitly states that Validation identifies violations while Governance resolves them and controls constraint evolution.

---

# 4. Extensibility Principles

Classification Extensibility follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Stability

Extensions shall preserve the stability of the Classification architecture.

An extension shall expand the architecture rather than undermine its foundations.

---

## 4.2. Semantic Preservation

Extensions shall preserve the established meaning of existing Classification Elements.

An extension shall not silently redefine an existing Family, Type or Class.

---

## 4.3. Structural Preservation

Extensions shall remain compatible with the canonical Classification structure.

New elements shall occupy positions permitted by the Classification Schema.

---

## 4.4. Backward Compatibility

Extensions should preserve the validity and interpretation of existing Classification whenever reasonably possible.

Existing documents should not become semantically ambiguous merely because Classification evolves.

---

## 4.5. Canonical Preservation

Extensions shall remain part of one canonical Classification architecture.

Independent competing Classification models shall not be introduced as extensions.

---

## 4.6. Technology Independence

Extension mechanisms shall remain independent of:

- programming languages;
- databases;
- repositories;
- serialization formats;
- implementation frameworks.

---

## 4.7. Controlled Evolution

Classification extensions shall be introduced through the applicable governance process.

An extension becomes canonical only after approval.

---

# 7. Extensible Classification Elements

The following Classification artifacts may be extended.

## 7.1. Classification Families

New Families may be introduced when a new high-level Classification domain is required.

An existing Family shall not be redefined to represent an unrelated domain.

---

## 7.2. Classification Types

New Types may be introduced within existing Families.

A new Type shall have a defined semantic relationship with its containing Family.

---

## 7.3. Classification Classes

New Classes may be introduced within existing Types.

A new Class shall comply with the semantic and structural constraints of its Type.

---

## 7.4. Classification Relationships

New relationship types may be introduced when an architectural requirement cannot be adequately represented by the existing relationship vocabulary.

Relationship extensions shall define:

- semantics;
- direction;
- source;
- target;
- cardinality;
- constraints;
- lifecycle implications.

---

## 7.5. Classification Schema

The Classification Schema may evolve through the controlled introduction of new structural capabilities.

Existing structural definitions shall remain valid whenever reasonably possible.

---

## 7.6. Classification Dictionary

The Classification Dictionary may be extended through the addition of newly approved Classification definitions.

Existing canonical definitions remain authoritative unless explicitly changed through governance.

---

## 7.7. Classification Specification

The Classification Specification may evolve to incorporate approved Classification extensions.

The Specification remains the normative integration point for the resulting Classification architecture.

---

# 8. Extension Categories

Classification extensions may belong to one of the following categories.

## 8.1. Additive Extension

Introduces new Classification Elements without changing the meaning of existing elements.

Example:

```text

            Existing Classification
            │
            ├── Family A
            │
            └── Family B

```

becomes:

```text

            Existing Classification
            │
            ├── Family A
            ├── Family B
            └── Family C   ←  Added

```

Additive extension is the preferred extension mechanism.

---

## 8.2. Specialization Extension

Introduces a more specific Classification Element within an existing semantic context.

For example:

```text

            Family
            │
            └── Type
                │
                └── New Class

```

The specialization must preserve the semantics of the parent context.

---

## 8.3. Structural Extension

Introduces an approved structural capability into the Classification Schema.

Structural extensions shall not invalidate existing Classification without explicit governance.

---

## 8.4. Relationship Extension

Introduces a new canonical relationship type.

For example:

```text

            Element A  ─────  newRelationship  ─────►  Element B

```

The new relationship shall have explicit semantics and constraints.

---

## 8.5. Dictionary Extension

Introduces new entries into the Classification Dictionary.

Dictionary extensions shall correspond to approved Classification concepts.

---

## 8.6. Specification Extension

Introduces normative requirements associated with an approved Classification capability.

---

## 8.7. Evolutionary Extension

Introduces a controlled refinement of the Classification architecture.

Evolutionary extensions may affect existing definitions and therefore require explicit impact analysis and governance.

---

## 4.2. Semantic Preservation

Extensions shall preserve the established meaning of existing Classification Elements.

An extension shall not silently redefine an existing Family, Type or Class.

---

## 4.4. Backward Compatibility

Extensions should preserve the validity and interpretation of existing Classification whenever reasonably possible.

Existing documents should not become semantically ambiguous merely because Classification evolves.

---

## 7.2. Classification Types

New Types may be introduced within existing Families.

A new Type shall have a defined semantic relationship with its containing Family.

---

## 7.3. Classification Classes

New Classes may be introduced within existing Types.

A new Class shall comply with the semantic and structural constraints of its Type.

---

## 8.7. Evolutionary Extension

Introduces a controlled refinement of the Classification architecture.

Evolutionary extensions may affect existing definitions and therefore require explicit impact analysis and governance.

---

# 23. Lifecycle Compatibility

Extensions shall integrate with the Classification Lifecycle.

A new Classification Element shall have an applicable lifecycle state.

Its lifecycle shall be governed in the same manner as existing Classification Elements.

Extensibility and lifecycle are complementary but independent concerns.

---

# 38. Extension Lifecycle

Extensions may themselves have a lifecycle:

```text

                 Proposed
                    │
                    ▼

               Under Review
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

The lifecycle state of an extension does not replace the lifecycle state of the Classification Elements introduced by it.

---

# 41. Extension Retirement

A retired extension is no longer part of the active Classification architecture.

Historical information associated with the extension should remain interpretable when necessary.

---

# 42. Non-Destructive Evolution

Classification evolution should prefer non-destructive mechanisms.

For example:

```text

         Existing Classification
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

               Replacement

```

is preferable to silently deleting an existing Classification Element when historical traceability is required.

---

# 43. Extension Compatibility with Historical Classification

An extension shall not make historical Classification unintelligible.

For example:

```text

           Historical Document
                    │
                    ▼

        Historical Classification
                    │
                    ▼

            New Classification

```

The new Classification may provide a replacement or supersession path without erasing the historical meaning.

---

# 35. Approved Extension

An approved extension becomes part of the canonical Classification architecture.

Conceptually:

```text

            Extension Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Approval
                    │
                    ▼

Canonical Classification

```

Before approval, the extension remains a proposal.

---

# 36. Rejected Extension

A rejected extension shall not become part of the canonical Classification architecture.

The rejection should preserve its rationale where governance traceability requires it.

---

# 1. Introduction

Classification provides the semantic organization through which documents are grouped into meaningful categories.

Within the Documentation Framework, Classification supports:

- organization;
- navigation;
- governance;
- discovery.

Classification is independent of the physical location of documents.

The Classification architecture therefore requires more than a formal model.

It also requires practices that preserve semantic clarity, structural consistency, maintainability and long-term architectural integrity.

Classification Best Practices defines recommended practices for designing, using, maintaining and evolving the Classification component.

This document is **informative**.

It provides guidance rather than introducing additional normative requirements beyond those established by the Classification architecture, constraints and specification.

---

# 1. Introduction

This document constitutes the normative specification of the Classification component within the Documentation Framework.

It consolidates the architectural principles, concepts, model, elements, schema, lifecycle, validation, governance, relationships, constraints, extensibility and terminology defined throughout the Classification documentation family into a single authoritative specification.

This document defines the contractual requirements that every Classification implementation shall satisfy in order to conform to the Documentation Framework.

Classification is an architectural mechanism for organizing documents according to meaningful semantic categories.

It is independent of physical document storage, implementation technology and repository structure.

---

## 6.1. R-001 — Architecture Compliance

Classification shall conform to the Classification Architecture defined by DF-CLS-001.

Classification implementations shall not introduce architectural responsibilities that contradict the Classification Architecture.

---

## 6.4. R-004 — Classification Model Compliance

Classification structures shall conform to the Classification Model defined by DF-CLS-003.

The model shall remain consistent with the conceptual foundation established by the Documentation Framework.

---

## 6.6. R-006 — Schema Compliance

Classification structures shall conform to the applicable Classification Schema defined by DF-CLS-005.

Schema requirements shall not be bypassed by implementation-specific behavior.

---

## 6.7. R-007 — Hierarchical Consistency

Where Classification uses hierarchical relationships, parent-child relationships shall represent meaningful semantic specialization.

An implementation shall not create artificial hierarchy solely for physical or technical convenience.

---

## 6.10. R-010 — Classification Assignment

A Classification assignment shall reference only valid Classification Elements defined by the applicable Classification Schema.

An assignment shall not introduce an undefined Classification concept.

---

## 6.13. R-013 — Cardinality Compliance

Classification assignments and relationships shall respect the cardinalities defined by the Classification Schema and Classification Constraints.

---

# 7. Semantic Requirements

Classification shall satisfy the following semantic requirements.

- Every canonical Classification Element shall possess one canonical meaning.
- Classification definitions shall remain stable.
- Equivalent Classification concepts shall not coexist without explicit semantic justification.
- Classification terminology shall remain consistent.
- Classification interpretation shall be deterministic.
- Classification relationships shall have explicit meanings.
- Hierarchical relationships shall represent meaningful semantic specialization.
- Classification shall remain independent of physical document organization.
- Classification shall remain independent of implementation technology.

These requirements derive from the Framework's requirement that architectural concepts be clearly defined, independent, stable, reusable and explicit.

---

# 8. Structural Requirements

Classification structures shall satisfy the following requirements.

## 8.1. Valid Elements

Every element shall be defined by the Classification model.

## 8.2. Valid Hierarchy

Every hierarchical relationship shall be structurally valid.

## 8.3. Valid Relationships

Every relationship shall conform to its defined relationship type.

## 8.4. Valid Cardinality

All applicable cardinality constraints shall be satisfied.

## 8.5. No Orphaned Canonical Elements

Every canonical Classification Element shall have a valid structural context unless the Classification Model explicitly defines it as an independent root element.

## 8.6. No Undefined References

Classification assignments and relationships shall not reference undefined elements.

---

## 6.5. R-005 — Element Compliance

Every Classification Element shall satisfy the characteristics defined by DF-CLS-004.

A Classification Element shall possess an identifiable semantic meaning.

---

## 6.20. R-020 — Semantic Stability

The semantic meaning of an active Classification Element shall remain stable.

A change that materially alters the meaning of an existing Classification Element shall be treated as an architectural change.

---

## 6.21. R-021 — Deprecation

A Classification Element that is no longer recommended for new use shall be capable of being placed into a deprecated lifecycle state.

Deprecation shall not silently erase historical Classification assignments.

---

## 6.22. R-022 — Historical Preservation

Historical Classification information shall be preserved where necessary to maintain the interpretation of previously established documentation.

Retirement shall not automatically imply deletion of historical meaning.

---

## 6.25. R-025 — Non-Destructive Validation

Validation shall not modify the Classification structure being evaluated.

Validation determines compliance; it does not silently correct the Classification model.

---

## 6.26. R-026 — Governance

Classification evolution shall occur only through the governance mechanisms defined by DF-CLS-008.

Significant architectural Classification changes shall be explicitly reviewed and approved.

---

## 6.27. R-027 — Governance Traceability

Governance decisions affecting Classification shall be documented and traceable.

The historical record shall identify the relevant change and decision.

---

## 6.29. R-029 — No Silent Redefinition

A Classification extension shall not silently redefine the meaning of an existing canonical Classification Element.

Semantic redefinition shall constitute an explicit architectural change.

---

## 6.30. R-030 — Backward Compatibility

Classification evolution shall preserve backward compatibility whenever reasonably possible.

Where compatibility cannot be preserved, the impact shall be explicitly identified and governed.

---

# 9. Lifecycle Requirements

Classification shall evolve according to DF-CLS-006.

Lifecycle transitions shall:

- be explicit;
- conform to the defined lifecycle;
- be traceable;
- respect governance;
- preserve historical meaning.

A typical lifecycle may be represented conceptually as:

```text

                 Proposed
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

The exact lifecycle states and transitions are defined by the Classification Lifecycle document.

---

## 6.24. R-024 — Deterministic Validation

Classification validation shall be:

- deterministic;
- repeatable;
- non-destructive.

The same Classification structure evaluated against the same rules shall produce an equivalent validation result.

---

# 33. Requirement Identification

Normative requirements are identified using the following format:

```text

    R-001
    R-002
    R-003
    ...

```

Requirement identifiers shall remain stable within a specification version.

When a requirement is removed or substantially redefined, its historical status shall remain traceable.

---

# 34. Requirement Interpretation

The following terms indicate normative strength:

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **shall** | Mandatory requirement |
| **shall not** | Mandatory prohibition |
| **should** | Recommendation unless a justified exception exists |
| **may** | Permitted behavior |
| **informative** | Non-normative guidance |

The terms **shall** and **shall not** identify mandatory requirements.

---

# 6. Relationship with Other Components

## 6.1. Metadata

Metadata provides descriptive information about documents that may participate in classification.

Classification uses that information without redefining the responsibility of Metadata.

---

## 6.2. Document Identity

Document Identity provides the logical identity of the documents to which classifications may be assigned.

Classification does not establish document identity.

---

## 6.3. Templates

Templates may define standardized structures for representing classification information.

Classification defines the semantic classification model rather than the template used to represent it.

---

## 6.4. Workflow

Workflow may use classification information when determining or controlling document processes.

Classification does not define workflow behavior.

---

## 6.5. Policies

Policies may establish rules governing the use or administration of classifications.

Classification provides the classification structures to which such policies may apply.

---

## 6.6. Registry and Discovery

Classification may provide semantic information used by Registry and Discovery mechanisms to organize and locate documentation.

---

## 6.7. Knowledge Graph

Classification concepts and relationships may contribute semantic information to the Knowledge Graph.

---

# 7. Documentation Structure

The Classification component is defined through the following documents:

| Order | Document | Description |
|------:|----------|-------------|
| 1 | DF-CLS-001 — Classification Architecture | Defines the architectural position, responsibility and boundaries of Classification. |
| 2 | DF-CLS-002 — Classification Concepts | Defines the fundamental concepts of Classification. |
| 3 | DF-CLS-003 — Classification Model | Defines the conceptual model governing classification. |
| 4 | DF-CLS-004 — Classification Elements | Defines the elements that constitute a classification system. |
| 5 | DF-CLS-005 — Classification Schema | Defines the formal structure of classification systems. |
| 6 | DF-CLS-006 — Classification Lifecycle | Defines the lifecycle of classification structures and assignments. |
| 7 | DF-CLS-007 — Classification Validation | Defines classification validation and conformance rules. |
| 8 | DF-CLS-008 — Classification Governance | Defines governance and control of classification systems. |
| 9 | DF-CLS-009 — Classification Relationships | Defines relationships between classification elements and related entities. |
| 10 | DF-CLS-010 — Classification Constraints | Defines constraints that preserve classification integrity. |
| 11 | DF-CLS-011 — Classification Extensibility | Defines mechanisms for extending classification systems. |
| 12 | DF-CLS-012 — Classification Best Practices | Documents recommended practices for classification design and maintenance. |
| 13 | DF-CLS-013 — Classification Dictionary | Defines authoritative Classification terminology. |
| 14 | DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification | Consolidates the normative Classification specification. |
| 15 | DF-CLS-015 — Classification Examples | Provides representative examples of Classification usage. |

---

# 10. Classification and Metadata Type

Metadata `Type` may participate in classification.

However, the semantic meaning of `Type` remains defined by Metadata.

Classification shall not redefine Metadata `Type` merely to support its own model.

The relationship between `Type`, semantic classification and physical organization shall be addressed consistently across the Documentation Framework.

In particular, the existence of physical directory distinctions shall not be interpreted as evidence that those directories define the semantics of `Type`.

---

# 14. Authoritative Specification

The complete normative definition of Classification is consolidated in:

**DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification**

The other Classification documents provide the concepts, models, structures, rules and supporting material from which the specification is established.

The specification is therefore the authoritative reference for the complete Classification component.

---

# 16. Roadmap

The development sequence of the Classification component is defined by:

**DF-RDM-030 — Classification Roadmap**

The roadmap describes the progressive development of the component but does not itself define the Classification architecture.

---

### 5.1.1. Dependency

Metadata→Document Identity remains the required declaration for identification of the applicable assigned normalized document described.

The functional DID README also states: “The Document Identity component depends on the Metadata component for the canonical definition of metadata concepts used to describe document identity.” Retain Document Identity→Metadata as an actual reciprocal required claim, not optional navigation. The exact README bytes/edition evidence and comparison source hashes are in the REVIEW/UPDATE map.

Responsible owners must reconcile which indispensable concepts/interfaces are required by identity core versus descriptive records, their exact governing editions and actual use. Different scope names alone do not dissolve a real required cycle. This UPDATE corrects the blanket denial of consumer dependencies; it does not certify that these reciprocal requirements are independent or globally reconciled.

---

## 5.2. Classification

Classification owns category meaning, distinct from the key of a classified normalized document.

---

### 5.2.1. Dependency

Classification→Document Identity is the required document-identification contract for an applicable assigned normalized document receiving classification. It is not a requirement that each category/definition/assignment entity has a DF document key.

---

### 5.2.2. Purpose

Classification categorizes the intended document under its own contracts. Family/Type/Component changes do not regenerate the stable allocated series/key. A category entity's identity and a normalized document describing that category are different subjects. Classification does not redefine document-key meaning.

---

# 7. Relationships with Discovery Components

The five original Discovery responsibilities remain separate from identity allocation and actual runtime delivery. Logical contracts may constrain projections and interfaces; actual availability, freshness and results need observations.

---

## 7.1. Registry

Registry→Document Identity is the required identification contract for document registrations. Registry owns registration/index records; Document Identity owns the underlying document-key meaning. Registry→Metadata is a selected descriptor contract in ARC-005§12. Repeated records/copies do not alone prove duplicate allocation. Record exact source editions, intended target/context, provenance and freshness. Registration is not allocation, approval or a mandatory intermediary for every consumer.

---

## 7.2. Relationships

Relationships owns connection type, direction, endpoints and connection records. For a document endpoint use the intended qualified document or exact edition/context under §4.4; other typed endpoints follow their own contracts. No rule here forces all possible associations to be document-to-document. Mutable connections do not redefine the key, and canonical endpoints alone do not prove a valid connection or permanently available target.

---

## 7.3. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph owns logical node/edge projection and representation contracts; storage/runtime technologies remain implementation choices. Knowledge Graph→Document Identity for document-node meaning and Knowledge Graph→Relationships for typed connections are selected required contracts in ARC-005§12. Neither is eliminated by calling the graph a projection.

Keep authoritative keys/connection sources distinct from projected records/properties. Nodes and properties may change while preserving intended qualified identity. Retain source edition/context, derivation, provenance, freshness and observed limitations. Projection does not allocate a new document identity, acquire connection authority or prove every peer representation is synchronized.

---

## 7.4. Navigation

Navigation uses intended identity and context to locate an applicable document or edition under its navigation contract. It can derive links and presentation records while preserving authoritative target meaning; the received prohibition on creating identity information means no competing allocation/semantic invention, not a ban on derived representation. Navigation does not guarantee successful current retrieval, require a universal Registry route or authorize silent retargeting.

---

## 7.5. Search

Search→Document Identity is the required identification contract for document-targeting search results. Other indexed entities retain their own endpoint contracts. Search owns query/result behavior, not document-key meaning. Record actual indexed source editions/context, target interpretation, freshness and result/retrieval observations. An index match does not prove allocation, complete population coverage, full identity validity or future availability.

---
